paragraphs.text: Greetings travelers and welcome to Goldbound, a brand new challenge series where gold is the only way out. Meet Goldilocked, a humble level one adventurer currently bound to Elwin Forest. He cannot leave, not until he earns enough gold to purchase a WoW token. Only then will he unlock a neighboring zone by the spin of a randomizer, but the curse will continue. And each new zone is locked until the next WOW token is earned. One man, one zone, one goal, escape. Today, we're going to find out if the beginning is a lucrative journey or a curse that will trap Goldilock in Elwin forever. Goldilock begins his quests by leveling up a little bit in Northshshire Valley. And time to lay down the ground rules.

Rule number one, we may only obtain items through quests, combat, looting, gathering, or crafting. Rule number two, we may trade out items with other players, but only for gold. No gear, no favors, just coin. For this purpose, we can sell items on the auction house. We simply can't purchase items on the auction house. Rule number three, Stormwind is technically a zone in Ellen Forest, and for our challenge, it's unlocked, but strictly for banking and auction house access. Rule number four, we may not leave the current zone until the gold goal is met. No stepping foot into Red Ridge, Westfall, or beyond until the price is paid. And rule five, the price we must pay is the live value of a WoW token. This will be a number that will fluctuate with the winds of the market over the entire challenge.

While I'm playing World of Warcraft for this series, I've got deep roots in old school Runescape, and I still love watching old school Runescape content to this day. And if you're familiar with that world, you've probably seen the Chunked Locked series. And this challenge is definitely inspired by that concept. Especially, I want to give a big shout out to Trader Steve, whose progression, buying expensive items to unlock new chunks, helped spark this very project. Of course, the WoW community has its own legends doing incredible zone locked content, and huge respect to Lord Nabble, Shacks, and Venario in particular, who are absolutely killing it with 100% zone completion runs. I'll drop their links in the description if you want to get more great content to check out because, hey, we're only on episode one, and we've got a long road ahead. And as we get grinding, make sure to subscribe so you don't miss episode two. And drop a comment below because for every zone we unlock, I'll be giving away a WoW token to a random subscriber and commenter.

One zone, one token, one goldbound journey. Let's get started. Our hero, Goldilock, has officially hit level 11, and we did it the oldfashioned way. Pure questing here in Ellen Forest. But while we were running around helping farmers and slaying cobalts, we quietly picked up something even more valuable. We've gathered a decent stash of herbs and ore. A mix of copper ore, peace, bloom, silver leaf, and earthroot. Not bad for a starting zone. But before we start listing anything, let's check on the WOW token price. Currently sitting at 261,000 gold. So yeah, we've got our work cut out for us. So we'll go ahead and start posting some of our items on the auction house. These early sales are really going to help kickstart our next gold making method, which fair warning is going to require a little startup capital, but this is what Goldbound is all about. Zone locked progress.

Creative gold farming and unlocking one WoW token at a time. Let's see what sells. We ran into a bit of a problem. Bag space. Turns out a bunch of the rare spawns in Elwin drop six to eight slot bags. And that means one thing. Goldilocked went onto a full-blown assassination mission. One by one, we tracked him down. Some gave us bags, some gave us bruises, but by the end of it, we walked away with a full set of bags. Now, while we were out bag hunting, some of our auctions sold. And just like that, our mailbox had 260 gold waiting for us. Not bad for level 11 with some basic gathering skills and a dream. And that timing couldn't be better because our next gold making method needs just a little startup capital. We made our way north to a very specific vendor, a mysterious woman known only as the crazy cat lady. Tucked away just outside of Stormwind, she sells rare and adorable cat pets. And people buy them. We picked up three of each. The black tabby, the white kitten, the Bombay cat, you name it. These vendor pets are limited in quantity and often get resold for 5 to 10 times the price on the auction house, especially for collectors and completionists. So, next stop, the auction house. We'll leave a few of these posted at all times and hopefully we have a few of them tick off while we're completing some more grinds in the zone. Now, as we start posting more and more items, you might have noticed I'm using an add-on called Trade Skill Master. This isn't for full automation or undercutting wars. It just helps me post auctions quicker and more efficiently as Goldilocks stockpile starts to grow. That way, we can spend less time at the auction house and more time out in Elwin forest making gold.

And speaking of Elwin, with bag space sorted in auctions rolling, it's time to get serious. We kicked off our first 1-hour dedicated gold farm circling Elwin forest in a large gathering loop. The goal is simple. Gather as many herbs and ore as possible while hitting every rare spawn along the way. Some of these rare mobs will drop a bind on equipped items that collectors will pay for big gold, but more on that later. For now, let's roll the montage. 1 hour later, our bags are full, the forest has been picked clean, and it's time to see what we've got. So, here's the final tally from our first 1 hour gathering. 214 copper ore, 85 Earthroot, 53 peace bloom, and 114 silver leaf.

Now, prices vary depending on the day, but these typically sell for about 3 to four gold on the auction house. So, let's crunch some numbers. Total material value is about 1,600 gold per hour. Not a bad starting place, especially since we only have a ground mount right now. But considering our goal is 260,000 gold for that WOW token, that's roughly a 220 hour grind. Uh-oh. But it's not all bad news. We also picked up a few bind unequipped green items worth between 50 gold each. None of the rare BOE's yet, but we'll be targeting specific mobs for those later. Now, here's where things got interesting. When I looked at the herb prices using TSM, everything looked pretty standard. You know, 3 to four gold for peace, bloom, silver leaf, earthroot. But when I looked at the mill value, it was showing something surprising. Over eight gold per herb.

That's because when you mill these low-level herbs with the inscription profession, you get alabaster pigment. This pigment is used in early crafting of glyphs and inscription recipes. It's not particularly rare, but the value adds up pretty fast. So, here's the trick. All the herbs in Alen Forest can be gathered with just level one herbalism. And milling these herbs only requires level one inscription. So, once I had some herbs, I just dropped herbalism, picked up inscription, and milled everything down. That one decision nearly doubled the profit on the herb portion of our 1-hour run from around 800 gold of raw herb value. We boosted up to 1,600 plus thanks to milling. Now, if you're looking to farm some gold yourself, maybe to grab your own WoW token, and you're not stuck in a zone lock challenge like I am, you'll want the most cutting edge, up-to-date gold making guides around. For that, check out Goldcap, your one-stop shop for gold strategies across retail, classic, and more. I'll leave a link down in the description. But for now, let's get back to Goldilocks. Slightly less efficient farming. I wanted to diversify the portfolio just a little, so I headed down to the local wararf, picked up fishing from the trainer, and grabbed the trusty fishing rod from a general goods vendor. For the next half hour or so, I stood by a small lake and fished my heart out, leveling up just enough to stop reeling in literal garbage. That magic moment hits at fishing level 30 when you can stop pulling in junk and start getting fish every cast. Raw brilliant small fish, long jaw mud snapper. The downside, well, these fish only sell for about 13 to 14 silver each. So, when you do the math, that's around six gold per hour. Not exactly gamechanging. Still, it was peaceful.

And hey, if Nat Pegle ever needs a break, I'm ready to sub in. But seriously, I do have a little fishing trick up my sleeve. If we're still stuck in Ellen when the Dark Moon Fair rolls into town, let's just say the fish might be worth a lot more. Until then, we'll leave the fishing to the pros. Around level 20, Goldilock started to hit a wall. Most of the quests were done, and the only leads left were breadcrumbs into Stormwind and Westfall. Both zones we can't access until we pay the gold toll. But then something unexpected happened. A little message popped up in chat reading, "You have learned expert riding." Wait, flying at level 20? I'll admit, I had no idea that was a thing in retail. Wow. Now, now, in the spirit of the gold bound challenge, or every gold matters and every advantage must be earned, I made a call. We went to the Griffin trainer, picked up a mount we already knew, paid 45 gold, and then promptly deleted it. That way, the gold was spent. No shortcuts, no freebies, just pure honest zone locked hassle. And with that, the skies were unleashed and it was time to retest the gold per hour for our gathering professions, now with an aerial advantage. So, we ran a nearly identical route as before. A full hour of herb and ore gathering with stops at every rare spawn that we could find. The results, seven mirror spawns, seven kills, some BOE's, a few vendor greens, and a couple low tier gems. The total looted item value came out to about 2.3k gold, which was nearly a 40% increase over the ground they run. But most of this did come from the rare spawn kills with the material breakdown only being slightly higher with 236 copper ore, 120 silver leaf, 82 earth, and 75 peace bloom.

Flying definitely shaved off some travel time, letting us hit more nodes and reach where our spawns faster and staying in motion. In the long run, flight is definitely going to mean more profit. So, our next gold farm is well, a little tricky. And I mean that literally because it's rogue only. At level 24, Goldilock finally unlocked Pigpocket and with it access to one of the sneakiest gold farms in Elwin Forest. Here's a secret. Almost every humanoid mob in Elwin that looks like they belong to a certain Westfall Brotherhood has a chance to drop a gray item called the frayed knot, but only through pickpocketing. Now, you might ask, why would a gray item that can't be equipped be worth anything? This particular knot is required to purchase the turquoise bobbleworm pet from Keeper Talhoot in Orios. It's part of a three item turnin.

the frayed knot, rabbit's foot, and large slimy bone. But here's the kicker. Goldilock can only farm the knot, and that's exactly what we're here to do. So, according to Wowhead, the drop rate for the frayed knot ranges from.3% to 8%. Depending on the mob, and it sells an average of 2.6 times per day, often going for 1 to 2,000 gold. So, just one sale per day could seriously move the needle on our goldbound grind. The mobs with the highest rates are the bandits, cutpurses, and even the rogue wizards in Elwin. My favorite pickpocket circuit includes the Brackwell pumpkin patch, Stone Karen Lake, and the encampments east of Westbrook Garrison. The trick is pockets reset every 10 minutes. So, with the right route, you can just loop back and start again, or kill them and let them respawn. That works, too. It's stealthy, it's smart, and it's completely off the radar for most players. As Goldilock continued the journey towards that coveted WoW token, the grind was in full swing. Herbs and ore gathered by the stacks, rare spawns hunted down, and every pocket picked clean for a few extra silver and a chance at the frayed knot. But with each loop through Elwin, we inched closer, not just in gold, but in level two. And eventually, we hit level 35. And that's when things got kind of weird. It seems that in these old classic retail zones, 35 is some kind of break point.

Suddenly, Goldilock was oneshotting just about everything. So lately, I've been running a tight rotation between Thoros, Lightfingers, Fed Fennel, and Mother Fang. They all have about a 25 to 30 minute respawn timer. So, in the meantime, I'm gathering herbs, mining ore, and pickpocketing anything with a red mask that moves. So far, we've racked up over 20 to 30 kills on each of these rares, but still none of the big ticket drops yet. No real jackpot, at least not yet. But since we've capped out our XP for this zone, feels like a perfect time to pause and do a full recap of our gold earnings and where Goldilock stands in that quest for that WOW token. If you know any sneaky gold farms in Elwin that we haven't hit yet, drop a comment below because I'd love to test them out. And right now, it seems like this triple threat is our best bet to get out of Elwin. All right, and here we are at the Goldshshire Inn. It's been our humble abode for the last quite a few days. And as you can see here at the bottom, we're about 22 hours into this challenge. So, we're going to go ahead and do a mailbox clear and see how much gold we actually ended up in this episode. So, over here, sold a few copper ore, some illusion dusts. Those are from selling the and disenchanting the greens as well as some alabaster pigments and inks. Excellent. So, a few gold coming in from those. Some more copper bars just to get more sales quickly. Some rough stones, more essences, a few one-off peace blooms and malchite. Just all gems here. Here's our first frayed knot coming through. So, 1.1k from that as well. Some more regular things.

Another frayed knot. There we go. And then here, a double frayed knot. See if I can actually see here. Just just says multiple buyers, I guess. I kind of wanted to show that it's not one of my characters buying those. And those do actually sell. Um, yeah, that's not my that is not my character. So, these are actually selling. Got quite a few fray knots out there. More copper ore. And let's just scroll through the TSM to see if anything else jumps out. Yeah, lots of frayed knots. We actually sold quite a few frayed knots here. Um, alabaster pigments that's from the herbalism. More alabaster, more frayed knots, lots of copper ore. So really, we'll go ahead and open all those, but really it's just that triple threat of getting the frayed knots, getting some herbs and ores, and killing some rares that we're we're using right now to get this gold. So that puts us right now just in Ellen Forest from a level one character, 23,898 gold on Goldilock. Real quick before we end up out the episode, WoW tokens are 257,000. So, we're about 10% there. But, we've really honed in the farms that really make this efficient.

But, like I said, if you know some farms in Alen Forest I haven't done yet, definitely drop a comment and uh I'll try those out for the next episode. And hopefully, we'll be unlocking one of the neighboring zones. So, for the challenge, we're going to be doing anything connected by a road, a ship, or a path. I'm genuinely curious how we'll have to adapt, how Goldilocks will handle the economy of a higher-level zone with other mobs, resource nodes, and danger at every turn. But that's what makes the adventure exciting.

So buckle up. Now we'll find out what Redridge has to offer. And, more importantly, what can we get out of it? And if you don't want to miss the continuation of this crazy journey, click the subscribe button. And to my fellow travelers, may the wind always blow at your back.

Drops like the Stone Splinter Axe, Stone Splinter Blade, and Stone Splinter Dagger. All of which fit the bill for solid zone transmogs. And then inside the cave down here with the Shamans and Bonesnappers, even more Stone Splinter gear of the Mace and Bracers. While none of these items are the holy grail of transmog in the zone, if we farm up a few of each, they will most definitely help stock the shelves for a while. But, one mob that maybe should have some legendary loot is the lock monster. I've definitely had some run-ins with this guy in classic, and he is now home in a much smaller pond, and unfortunately, he doesn't drop anything at all. Speaking of legendary drops though, how about an update on Molten Core? We are on to run 31 of Molten Core, and still no second binding, and no Nightslayer Chest. Seriously, we didn't leave empty-handed because the Eye of Sulfuras dropped from Rag. This is the legendary component eventually needed for Sulfuras, Hand of Ragnaros, the legendary two-handed mace. Of course, Goldie can't wear it, but it would still be cool to get and craft for Golden Path, our paladin crafting alt with blacksmithing. So, once Arcanite Bars are unlocked with Tanaris alchemy vendors, we can look into this a little bit closer. At At know the drop tables aren't totally bugged in Molten Core for now though. But I do want to test a little bit of skinning in Loch Modan and in this zone there is really only one skinning farm that jumps out and it's because it's kind of looped up with a transmog farm. The target though, the black bears. And this one is kind of interesting because if you ever played through Loch Modan back in the day in classic, you might remember the horde patrol that walked down the east side of Loch. Well, they weren't just there to kill alliance players and they actually had some pretty solid loot on their tables.

The bastion pauldrons and the orcish cleaver. Except those mobs were removed from the zone and now these black bears have both those drops on their tables. The bastion pauldrons are worth anywhere from 8 to 32,000 gold and the orcish cleaver has a market value around 49,000 gold. Although a sale average closer to 3K, but a decent little farm for sure. And maybe if paired with skinning, we can get a little bit of trade good gold per hour as well. The bears themselves do hyper spawn. Technically, they just have a very large area over which they spawn. So we have to kill all the way from the south of Thessalmar all the way up to north mountain range to get them to hyper spawn. And the loot? Well, we've gotten pretty lucky on the transmog, but honestly, as far as skinning goes, the current value of light leather, the gold per hour of raw trade goods was only about 700 gold per hour on these guys and I think we might be better off just not skinning the bears and instead getting more kills for more chances at the transmog. We'll probably just stick to dual gathering for consistent farming. Well, probably because there is one more kind of skinning farm that I do want to try. I say kind of skinning because it's actually using the engineering skill.

Yeah, there is this cave, kind of approaching the badlands border, that has mechanical chickens and whatnot. I honestly didn't know this cave was here before, but as long as we have engineering, after we kill the mobs, we can actually disassemble these guys for spare parts. Yeah. On testing it though, well, it works out to be about seven gold per hour. We really only get any value from the silver contact that can drop from these, but it is quite the rare drop off scrapping and the rest is just low value vendor trash. And we can't even kill them that fast because they also don't hyper spawn, so we just end up fishing in the back of the cave. And ultimately, I think most of the gold of the seven gold per hour comes from fishing up lock frenzies. And on the topic of fishing, there is still technically a lock, one that we can fish in. And of course, during Darkmoon Faire, which is now active, we can use our Darkmoon fishing hat here and also throw a few lines into the local schools, sagefish schools. These are the same fish pools that we had in Redridge and Stranglethorn and even a few in Westfall. So nothing particularly new, but I will at least use this area to maximize a few Darkmoon Firewaters. And as we're exploring more and more of Loch Modan, we're getting a pretty good loop around here. Doing a gathering, checking in on rare spawns. Plus it never hurts to drop down on the tunnel rat scouts or the ogres, the mobs that don't hyper spawn, and try to get a few of those big ticket items. And we've gotten a few.

And at least for now, it's a pretty reliable way to maximize the farms in the zone, a little bit of a lock frenzy itself. But like I said, I have been getting quite a bit of transmog from this zone. Our shelves are definitely full with new Loch Modan gear to sell, and I have been doing plenty of undercut scans to keep them competitive. So I think it's about that time for a mailbox clear. Let's see what the progress is. Checking on the WoW token price, it is at just under 259k. And we only have 3.6k right now. So let's hope for some solid loot. The trade goods weren't too wild in Loch Modan, so let's go ahead and waste no time and gets these all looted up.

And that puts the clear at just over 26,000 gold of trade goods, putting us up to 29k. But Loch Modan was a transmog angle for sure, so let's go check on that. And a few transmog pieces selling for sure. But you might notice no Loch Modan gear. And that's because I actually sent that over to a different hidden alt, just so we can see how much value we got from the backlog transmog, and how much we got from Loch Modan transmog. Now, the backlog was pretty darn good to be fair, quite a few sales coming through here, and loots up for a total of about 24.8 thousand gold. But we should go check the other alt with Loch Modan and a few other unique items that I want to keep a bit more hidden and undercut more frequently on. And well, we sold some Loch Modan stuff for sure. Amongst something else as you can see, the Mogorok's Toothpick and the Rodentia's Shortsword.

But yeah, we got to talk about it because Stealth Blade sold. Let's go. We had to sell it at the competitive price of 275k. It took quite a few reposts and undercuts, but that alone is literally a WoW token. So, let's get all 308k of this haul looted and over to Goldie. There we go. 360k in the bags. Enough for even an EU token right now. And all combined, we got about 80,000 gold from the lock with a good chunk, about 29k coming from lock button transmog, about 26k from trade goods, and about 25k from backlog transmog. This does mean we can buy a new token and right away roll a new zone, which we'll do live here on YouTube next Monday 10:00 a.m. Mountain Time, or you could tune in over on twitch.tv/pathofexilegold if you prefer watching there. Until next time, go with honor, friend.

paragraphs.text: Greetings travelers, and welcome back to Goldbound, where our rogue Goldilocked is unlocking the map of Azeroth one zone at a time. Each new zone unlocked by the spin of a wheel paid for by a WoW token purchased by gold farming in our currently unlocked zones. We are slowly working our way through Eastern Kingdoms with more and more of the map being available week after week. And today is no different because last episode we were locked to the lock, Loch Modan that is, and we optimized the transmog, trade goods, and sold our way up to a new WoW token. Albeit with a little help from one of our biggest, if not the biggest, transmog piece selling stealth blade. So, with a new WoW token loaded up in the bags, let's have a quick look at the map to see where our next zone spin can send us. We still do have the option of sailing over to Kalimdor through the Booty Bay boats to the Barrens, which would open up a whole lot more zones on the western side of the map including two Horde starting zones pretty soon, Mulgore and Durotar. So, some interesting aspects if we roll Barrens.

In the south of Eastern Kingdoms though, we still have Deadwind Pass waiting to be rolled. This is one of the longest standing zone rolls that we still haven't hit, not to mention maybe the biggest wild card. A little further north we have the Badlands connected to Loch Modan and home to some pretty solid farms and high-level materials. And lastly, the most recent addition to the available zones to roll connected only by Loch Modan, the Wetlands. A spin here would send us even further north into the Eastern Kingdoms and put a few new zones onto the spinner. So, we have a lot of map to uncover, so let's get right into the spin. Wetlands at the first opportunity. We are making some crazy progress north in Eastern Kingdoms and we have almost half of all of Eastern Kingdoms unlocked so far. Pretty sweet. Let's head over to Wetlands to see what it has to offer. We do enter the zone through the tunnels accessible from Loch Modan just north of Dun Algaz. It seems like most of our zones right now are being unlocked through these dwarven built tunnels. So, let's get exploring. Now, this zone, Wetlands, was changed quite a bit during Cataclysm much like Loch Modan. So, some of the key areas do look a little bit different than in classic, but we do have the Dun Algaz area, Green Warden's Grove, a new elf area, Swiftgear Station, and of course, Menethil Harbor.

Taking on a little bit of water it seems. More than that though, we have some gold farms. And while I do know a couple of gold farms in Wetlands, to be completely honest, I haven't farmed in this zone specifically in a quite a while. So, Goldy's exploration here is going to take quite a bit of research, loot table scouring, and feet on the ground to find out some more farms. But, I did say I knew a couple. And the first thing that comes to mind for me is Wetlands whelp farming. That's right. Much like the bronze whelp of Blasted Lands and dark whelps in Burning Steppes, we have a few more whelps here. Two actually. There is the OG Tiny Crimson Whelpling, a classic battle pet, one that could drop in Wetlands way back in the day from the flame snorting whelps around here. If you watched the last Double Down Burning Crusade video I did, this was the last battle front for Double Down to try to make his double.

Unfortunately, in that challenge, our time was limited and we did not get the whelp to drop. In retail though, those flame snorting whelps are actually gone. However, all is not lost because the Tiny Crimson Whelpling has turned into somewhat of a zone wide drop here. Pretty much all of the mobs across all of Wetlands post Cataclysm have this pet on their loot tables. The downside, well, it is a very low drop rate, 0.01 for most mobs making it about a one in 10,000 drop. So it is on the table for pretty much every killing farm we do which is much like the stranglethorn Vale zone drops of the Hyacinth macaw and pirate hat. That being said, I do have a little bit of a trick up my sleeve for Wetlands. One that should increase our zone kills per hour pretty drastically, but let's not jump into that yet because I did say there were two welps available here. There's also the dark whelp playing courtesy of the Ebon welps in the zone. These welps seem to have actually replaced the spawn locations of the previous flame snorting and crimson welps in classic. And speaking of which, they do still have the zone drop of the crimson whelp one in 10,000, but they also have the dark whelp at a much more reasonable point oh nine percent drop rate. So closer to one in 1,000. Now we're getting somewhere.

They do have a pretty big spawn location so we can run around this general eastern location pretty aimlessly killing welps over and over. Even though it's still a one in 1,000 drop, it is worth farming because the dark whelp carries a market value of 50,000 gold and a sale average closer to 10,000 gold. Pretty solid. And if you're thinking this pet sounds pretty familiar, well, it's because it is. This is the exact same whelp that we could actually loot in Burning Steppes. One that we did loot and we did sell for about 9,000 gold I believe. So let's get out there farming going for another one. And while we're killing these Ebon welps for the pet, we have a few more items that we can actually snag from them. Oh yeah. This is a little bit of a multi farm. Let's talk with the obvious first.

It's kind of a skinning farm albeit kind of slow. The welps skin into either light leather or medium leather respectively about one to five gold each. On top of that, we can also get black whelp scales. These are currently valued about one to four gold each depending on the day. So each base kill on a whelp is about three to eight gold of leather. So, they do have some consistent trade good drops and for regular rates, which is always good when we're farming a super rare drop because most times if you farm this for an hour, we're not going to get the whelp, but at least we'll walk away with one to 3,000 gold in skinning materials. To really juice the skinning, there is another farm I want to try that it will probably give more gold per hour. Look at that later though because it doesn't end here for the Ebon whelps. They don't just have the whelp and they don't just have skins. They also have the Smoldering Set on their loot tables. Now, a few different mobs around Wetlands drop different pieces of this transmog set, but the Ebon whelps drop the boots, which have a market value of about 11,000 gold and an average sale price of 400 gold. They also drop the Smoldering Gloves, a little bit better with a 15k market value and a 1,000 average sale.

So, we won't be upset if we snag a few of these pieces. And oh, we snagged quite a few. The drop rate seems to actually be pretty decent on these and we'll target the rest of the set as well, but that's from other mobs in the zone. Starting off, I think I'm liking the Ebon whelp farm. And speaking of which, after not much farming, boom, the Dark Whelp Ring. Again, and pretty lucky for one of our first drops because we got this looted before kill 300, not even an hour of farming. And with it being a one in 1,000 drop rate, I would say a little bit on the lucky side. Very good. Now, one thing I usually do whenever we go into a new zone on Goldbound is check and see if the borders are clean or if there's a new zone bordering our current zone that might accidentally be explored. You know, after the Westfall to Duskwood border incident. So, hopping on to Path of Exile here, my main who can freely cross any borders, I found a couple potentially troublesome spots.

Up in the mountains bordering Twilight Highlands, just above this cave, if we fly too high, even where it looks like it's still Wetlands, maybe if we see a mining node up here or something, boom. It swaps over to Twilight Highlands. That's a little dangerous, but good to know. Possibly more dangerous, though, is out by the coast, north of Swiftgear Station, because for some reason about 50 ft of this coastline or more is coded in the game as a Wrath of the Highlands. Yeah, that could have been a very easy accidental forfeit zone, kind of like our Darkmoon Faire adventure. With such wishy-washy borders here, it's probably worth mentioning that I am going to set two forfeit zones before an accidental zone lock on happens. Hopefully it doesn't, but if I do accidentally explore a locked zone, like either of the Highlands at the moment, well, if it happens in Eastern Kingdoms, the forfeit zone is going to be Fashir, just off the coast.

Once we get to Kalimdor, any accidental explorations there are going to be the forfeit zone of Deepholm. Again, just off the coast of Kalimdor. The rationale here is that these are two zones that won't come up on the regular zone spins, like the other Cataclysm zones of Highjal and Twilight Highlands. There is just no paths leading straight into the water, so we'll have to get them eventually, and I think this is the best way to have them as a possibility. If I accidentally discover a locked zone, it's relegation to a forfeit zone for 1 week, or until a new wow token is earned, whichever comes first. Pretty much exactly what we did with Darkmoon Faire. Let's hope it doesn't happen here in Wetlands, though, because I'm having a lot of fun discovering some of these farms. Take the cave beside the dangerous Twilight Highlands potential unlock, for example. Luckily, the cave itself in the mountain is unlocked and coded as Wetlands through and through, because there are some things that are definitely worth farming in this cave.

First and foremost, there's a rare spawn, the Razormaw Matriarch. And this rare spawn has quite a few decent transmog drops, and two very solid transmog drops, like the Jurassic wristguards. Market values on these bracers float anywhere between 40,000 and 100,000 gold with average sale price being 5,000 gold. So, a good drop for sure. Then, there's also the Beaded Raptor Collar, another solid transmog piece with a value of 10 to 80k, but a bit lower on the average sale price around 1,000 gold. Still a good one to tag. But, we aren't just here for the rare because she also guards a nest. And as far as I know, the nest does have an independent spawn from the rare, but it can contain an egg, the Razormaw Hatchling, which is actually just a pet, one that can be sold for upwards of 1,000 gold. So, yeah, we'll most definitely pop into this cave every now and then and try our luck at the rare spawn and the egg spawn. And if you're counting, which we are, that is three high-value battle pets from the Wetlands so far, and we aren't even done with the battle pets here just yet. Now, the rest of the cave here does have some raptors, and since we currently have skinning, we can check and see what they drop. There isn't anything crazy on their loot tables, but we can snag a few more medium and light leather from these guys.

Oh, well, I guess we can always get blue world drops, no matter what the drop tables say. We just pulled the Raptor's Edge, a blue world drop BOE. Maybe a higher drop rate from raptors, I don't know, but it does have a market value of 6,000 to 17,000 gold. A very nice drop from here. Not exactly something we can specifically target for again, but a good one to get while testing. And into the bags and onto the auction house it goes. So far, we've spent most of our time here in the Wetlands on the east, but there's also a few things over in the west that are worth checking out. Over at Welgar's Retreat and Welgar's Excavation Site, we have a few things going on because there's some rock elementals, Paleolithic elementals, plus some living fossils.

It's quite the archaeology site over here, but I'm really just after the elementals because these guys are one of the mobs that after being killed can be mined for some resources. Now, I'm thinking they might make a pretty decent trade good farm. Their base drop of trade goods contains elemental earth and core earth. That's before even mining them. Both of these trade goods don't have crazy value though, around three to four gold for the elemental earth and 50 silver for the core of earth. Not crazy, but any gold helps. And once they're killed and looted, we can mine them. And here, they actually give some pretty decent drops. First up is one to two tin ore, not too bad, probably one to two gold each. The real ticket price here though is that 30% of the time they mine into one to two iron ore. And with iron ore prices over five gold right now, that could add up pretty fast. So, the trade goods are definitely the angle from these guys, but of course, it's a mob in the Wetlands, so we're constantly rolling on tiny crimson welping drops, blue BOEs, and just regular old transmog. The living fossils around here, the dinosaurs, don't really have any good trade goods like the elementals, and we can't mine or skin them. So, for the farm, I am mostly just skipping them, although they could drop the welp. And while the elementals are pretty spread out over here, down in the dig site and up the ramp all the way up into a cave, if we do a big circle of all of their spawn locations, killing and mining all the elementals, they do eventually hit a forced spawn and we can farm them indefinitely. In this case, using our outlaw rogue and grappling hooks to safely get down from the cave area back to the base of the dig site when they start respawning.

This farm actually raises a pretty good point because archaeology is actually a skill and a secondary profession in World of Warcraft, but we haven't had a chance to use it yet. The reason? Well, there's just no archaeology trainers in our currently unlocked zones. They're only in major cities in Eastern Kingdoms, which we don't have access to those trainers yet. But, Wetlands opens up an archaeology trainer on the roll over in Kalimdor in Dustwallow Marsh. There's an archaeology trainer there. So, if we do roll that zone, this whole thing, as far as archaeology, may now be on the table. And while archaeology might not be a crazy gold farm, we'll have to wait to see. Once we get archaeology training, we will definitely test it out to see if we can make some coin or at the very least get some upgrades for Goldie from it. Anyways, back to the numbers. How was the gold per hour from farming the elementals?

Well, after an hour of farming, we managed to pull in 171 iron ore, not bad, 167 tin ore, 31 cores of earths, and 34 elemental earths. And we actually snaked up 11 essence of earths, which I didn't see on the drop tables, but those are only one gold each anyways. All in all, the trade good value here came out to 1,322 gold per hour. Not amazing, and during this farming hour, we didn't pull in the crimson whelpling either. All this talk with the whelpling though, I think we better get back to a farm that is going to pull in one eventually. One that I can imagine many of you are waiting for me to do, the classic Wetlands hyper spawn farm. So, down to the east of Greenwarden's Grove in the green belt, kind of right in the middle of the spawn location of the even whelps, we have two warring mobs, the even slave hunters and the Dragonmaw Whelp Stealers. And if we stand right in the middle here, where the two forces are clashing, as long as we respect for AoE, we can kill five of the mobs that are fighting, and within 10 seconds or less, five new mobs rush up to take their place. Oh, yeah. This is a no moving, highly AFK-able hyper spawn farm. And there's a few things to farm here.

First, of course, and kind of the reason we're here, is the tiny crimson whelpling. It's just a zone drop, and this is probably the easiest spot in the zone to get thousands of kills without too much trouble. So, staying here for a few hours is going to dramatically increase our zone-wide kill count and slowly work towards that one in 10,000 drop. But, on top of that, the slave hunters are dragonkin. They can be skinned. Yeah. And during the hyper spawn, between killing and looting, we pretty much have an infinite skinning farm. They just keep spawning, we keep killing and skinning. Now, they only give light leather and medium leather, which are still one in five gold each respectively, but with how many we should be able to kill per hour, it might end up being a very good consistent trade good farm, too. Plus, every kill here rolls the dice on the tiny crimson whelpling. But, that whelp isn't all that's on these guys' loot tables. They also have a few more pieces of the smoldering set, the chest and the legs.

Like the rest of the set, we can't really expect any crazy values from them, but good nonetheless, and we do get a lot of them. For example, I think I've already gotten 10 of the smoldering chests here, and I've only farmed for about 2 hours. So, some of those will go on the auction house, and some I'll just vendor. Aside from that, though, one of the best transmog pieces we can get, and one I actually just pulled in, is the buccaneer's chest piece. A classic romance novel-looking chest piece and a staple in the transmog world. Massive sale averages, super good sale rates, so I'm expecting this one to move probably for 10 to 15k, and probably pretty quickly. But, with how rare the whelp and the buccaneer's chests are, even with how many kills we're getting, we can't expect to get a whelp or a good piece of gear every hour, which isn't too bad, though, because they also drop a decent amount of low-value greens, mostly stuff that we'll vendor for the five to 15 gold vendor sale price, but also a good amount of raw gold, just coins. Plus, a consistent supply of wool cloth, linen cloth, and even some silk cloth. And well, of course, the skins as well.

Speaking of the cloth though, for some reason these guys don't actually seem to be affected by open world anti-hyper spawn mechanics. Maybe something to do with the way they're being pulled, the fact that they're fighting, but either way it makes this a crazy good farm. And in this case, with fan of knives, rogue is actually pretty good for AOEing and I am using darkmoon firewater to skin them faster and keep up with the skins because without it we tend to fall behind and skins go to waste. But the gold standard for this farm is definitely monk. Brewmaster monk actually because they have a good AOE and they can place their taunt statue in some strategic locations to pull the packs around. The ones that I can't pull as a rogue. So they can nearly double their kills per hour. And technically speaking, the gold standard monk race would probably be worgen since their skinning speed buff would allow them to keep up with the higher amount of mobs they can kill. But for us, a lonely rogue, I figure it's best to place a number on the raw gold and trade good value from these guys. And then just take the big drops like the welps or buccaneer's chests as a bonus if they come. So after an hour of farming and testing this hyper spawn, I actually managed to pull in 537 light leather, our best light leather farm in the game so far, 385 medium leather, 309 wool cloth, 54 silk cloth, plus a few light and medium hides. On top of that, we got 140 gold in looted currency from these mobs and 380 gold in vendor trash, giving us a raw total consistent gold per hour just north of 4,000 gold per hour. And like I said, that isn't even counting transmog sales, buccaneer's chests, and crimson whelp chances. After a few hours of farming this though and over 3,000 kills, still no whelp, but we'll come back here a lot to farm for sure. But we can't just stick to one farm for the entire zone even if the farm here looks pretty good. But that's all right because there are a few other locations I want to farm. Take the Angerfang encampment for example.

There's a few assorted Dragonmaw here. The ones we want to farm though are the Centurions. Although to get these guys to spawn reliably, we kind of just kill every Dragonmaw on site here. But the Centurions in particular can drop the Dragonmaw Shortsword. This transmog weapon comes in with a ticket price of about 40,000 gold. But postings are pretty sparse on it. And average sales are pretty low. So I don't know what a realistic sale price would be. Likely two to 4,000 gold. But while we're roaming around looking for Centurions, there's also a rare spawn here to keep an eye out for. Garneg Charrskull. Plus his drop of the Ringing Helm. Another 40K transmog piece that could likely fetch some good coin on the auction house. Ironically though, while farming here for a while, neither of these are the drops that I got. I guess maybe Wetlands has a high drop rate of world drop blues because boom.

The Darksteel Bastard Sword. A blue two-handed sword BOE zone drop. And I mean, look at this thing. This is a sword I would definitely want to have in battle. And it's also a sword that I want to have on the auction house. With a market value of 150,000 gold. Yep. You heard that right. My hearing stealth blade 2.0. Although I doubt a sale would hit market value on this. It's a pretty high ticket. But I would definitely expect at least 20 to 50,000 gold for this bad boy. And so far Wetlands is delivering. Well, maybe it's all the saved up luck from Molten Core because run 33 and still no Nightslayer Chest and no second binding. Either way though, we only just got into Wetlands this week. But we've already snagged up a few valuable solid battle pets, two world BOE blues, tons of skins, and even some consistent ore farms. So let's go ahead and check the mailbox clear to see how much movement we we have.

Current price of the wild token is sitting around 261k and our current cash stack is 109,000 gold. Let's see the trade good haul here. Okay, okay. Quite a bit of variety. Well, we haven't been doing too much trade goods. So, let's get this all looted up and see where we're sitting at. About 30,000 gold total and we're up to 138k, but let's see how the transmog has done. And okay, not bad, but no massive items this week and none of the welps moving either. So, let's get this thing looted up, get it over to Goldie, and get back up there to farm some more gold. Get a few more hours and hopefully a tiny crimson whelpling. Until next time, go with honor, friend.

paragraphs.text: Greetings travelers, and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where a rogue Goldilocked is exploring the world of Warcraft by unlocking one zone at a time. And recently, that zone was the Wetlands, which means we've a very solid chunk of Eastern Kingdoms unlocked, but a whole lot of gold left to farm. Because the current cash stack after last week's mailbox is just sitting over 150k with a WoW token hovering between 250 and 270,000 gold recently. So, the question today, can we harvest over 100,000 gold from the Wetlands this week and purchase another WoW token to roll a new zone? Well, let's find out. And travelers, welcome back to the Wetlands. And if you recall, last week in the Wetlands we got quite a few good drops, some world BOE blues, and the Ebon Whelp. But, there was one whelp that we didn't loot up. The zone drop Crimson Whelp. So, I've been spending a good chunk of my spare time at the intersection trying to hyper spawn these mobs to increase my chances at loot. And travelers, oh, we got the whelp in the bags. paragraphs.text: Greetings, travelers, and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where our rogue Goldilocked explores Azeroth, unlocking one zone at a time. I've been sending all the drops over to my secret 1,000 needles transmog toon, so everything on that character is from this zone. Let's go ahead and see what the auction house looks like. All right, so we have 333 items listed with a total value of over 1.9 million gold. Kind of crazy. Now, some of this is from zone drops and the Saltstone Cave, so it's not all RFD, but still, we pulled in an insane amount of gold in during the zone. Let me show you some of the bigger drops. First up and the biggest one, we do have the Broken Blade of Heroes. This thing is kind of a blacksmithing recipe, but a one-time use and has a value between 40,000 and 1 million gold. I do have it listed for a relatively aggressive price of about 125,000 gold, but it can also be reforged into the blade with a classic blacksmith. The blade does have similar competition and listing prices though, so I figured I would see if I could get a quick sell on the broken blade before maybe reforging it on the crafting alt. We also pulled in a ton of the Saltstone set though, pretty much everything but the leg chains and maybe the van braces to be honest, which to be fair, are the most expensive pieces. Then we also got a few assorted dungeon BOEs like the freezing shard from RFD. Of course, we are also trying to quick sell the Marauder Scimitar while we're in the zone. And then the Straw Gale Fists, Briar Tredders, and Thought-Kast Boots. Beyond that, RFD just literally prints out an insane amount of moderate value greens.

Things in the two to 30,000 gold bracket. I mean, just look at all these listings. I only list two at a time maximum to save on auction house fees, but we are definitely rolling here. So, it's fair to say we have pulled in a crazy amount of item value in the zone, but how fast can we sell it? So, I'm out here farming turtles in the Saltstone Cave, still looking for the elusive leg chains, of course. But man, I must say, I didn't expect it, but 1,000 Needles might be my favorite gold bound zone so far. There is just such crazy value between the zone drops and rares, not to mention the dungeon and the turtles. Well, you can't beat a turtle farm. So, I've been doing some relisting, undercut scans, and trying to get some stuff moving here. Let's go ahead and pop into the trade good auctions and see how much we made this week for Goldie.

Who knows? Maybe we'll have enough to spin for a new zone already. First things first, we've actually pulled in 14,857 raw gold, which is mostly from RFD runs, and the token is at 267,000 gold. Let's see how we did. 170 auctions here for trade goods, and even a few fire water coming in from the last couple of days. Just using the Darkmoon Hat off cool down actually yielded 2.3k. Not bad. Then of course, some herbs and some skins. Let's get this all added up and see where the trade good tally lies. But to be fair, I did spend a lot more time doing transmog here than consistent gold. Okay, so we're up to just over 60,000 gold with about 47,000 gold from trade goods, which does seem a little bit light, but ah, yeah, so it looks like the turtle farm is encountering some undercutters. I'll make sure I undercut scan more frequently and repost these to hopefully move it pretty quick. And let's go check the transmog alts. First one, the backlog. And it looks like we've been selling a good amount of lower value transmog here, which makes sense. I mean, the Trial of Style was this week, so some cheaper inventory is probably moving.

Oh, well, that's nice. We sold the skull plate bracers for 100,000 gold. These are the ones a blue BoE that we got back in Aldaman. And I mean, that's a pretty good ticket price for them. Also, an Orb of Deception. I'm thinking this might be a pretty good transmog week after all. So, let's get this alt loaded up and see where it stands. 133,000 gold. Not a bad week for the backlog tune. But, how about the 1,000 needles alt? I have been reposting a little bit more aggressively on this one. Ah, well, we can't always get the sales, I guess. It is what it is, and transmog is definitely a long game. So, we just have to keep building up the backlog alt, which I guess this is already paying dividends. So, with it all back on Goldie here, we are up to 196,000 gold and in just about 60,000 gold short from the token. But, to be fair, we do have about 20,000 gold in trade goods waiting to be sold and a new awesome farm to run. Not to mention, a literal ton of transmog to sell. So, we might be spinning sooner than expected. Until then, we'll go with honor, friend.
Hey.
