paragraphs.text: Hello, travelers, and welcome back to Goldbound—a series of challenges where our rogue Goldilocks explores Azeroth, discovering one location at a time. Each new location unlocks once we earn a WoW token, which is around 270,000 gold in our current zones. Last time we stopped by to check the mail, with just over 100,000 gold in Arat, but also auctioned off a very valuable item—the Shadowcaster's Mantle. So, before we start farming, I think it's worth checking our email to see how much gold we actually need for the token . That's all. They bought a robe. I lowered the price relative to the regional one to sell faster—it came out to about 285,000 gold, which is more than needed for the token and to open the next zone. In addition, I made another 29,000 from selling transmog items from leftovers, mostly thanks to the Bluegill Kukri and Dark Iron Gauntlets. And this means that we can play a new location. But before that, before I get too caught up in the process, I want to complete the weekly raids in the already open areas. In addition, we need to discuss available locations. When it comes to weekly raids, we have two main ones.

First, Onyxia's Lair for a mount. What's up this week? Nothing. The drop chance is very low, so we'll keep running there, hoping to eventually replace our Ghostly Gryphon. And, of course, Fiery Bowels. We are still hunting for the Windseeker's Left Link for Thunderfury, the Windseeker's Blessed Blade, and the Nightslayer's Breastplate. So while I'm running, let's talk about the areas that could drop today. Here, in the Eastern Kingdoms , there are many old acquaintances. There is Dead Wind Pass, the area that has remained undiscovered for the longest time. She has already avoided our choice 14 times. Maybe I'll get lucky today. To the north, the Twilight Highlands still remain. This is an interesting option with Cataclysm-era raids and dungeons, as well as good resource farming. Further north, thanks to the discovery of Arati, the Gilsbrad Foothills are now accessible. There are interesting places to farm there, the Alterac Mountains, and a path further north to the continent.

And then there's the Inner Lands, where three of our four archaeology points are now located. Next, on Kalimdor, we have two zones. First, the Steppes, which connect us to many other zones, including two upcoming starting locations. And just south of the Cave Marsh, we have the Thousand Hawks, which are the true gateway south to Cenarion, Un'Horo, and Silithus. So, these are the results of our throws, but what about the loot? Well, again 41 passes of the Fiery Core, and no second binding, and again no Nothing Killer breastplate. Maybe we'll get lucky next week, which means all we have to do is choose a new zone.

Okay, okay, Thousand Hawk. So, we're back in Kalimdor, and this zone adds two new Kalimdor zones to our list for next time. But first, before we head out there and get to work, we have a lot of extra gold left over from selling the robes. So I'll just put this in the squad bank, where we put the surplus from each zone to build up for the next bank deposit. We have already accumulated over a thousand gold, and the next tab costs 500 thousand. So, we're actually pretty close. Anyway, we're back in the Cave Swamp, and it's time to enter Thousand Hawk to see how good or bad the gold mining is in that area. So, welcome to Thousand Hawks. If you have n't played in a while, this area will definitely look completely different from what you remember. To begin with, almost the entire valley floor is now underwater. This, in itself, has both pros and cons, but more on that later. But now, thanks to the water, we have Fizzle and Pozzik's speed barge.

So the salt marshes that Fizzle had previously traveled through turned into a kind of floating expedition. Additionally , there is the Twilight Weatherling, the High Perch, perhaps surprisingly, the dungeon of Iglyph Barrow, and the Southsea Fortress, home to the Admiral's Lair, also known as the Saltstone Cave. As for the farms in this area that I know about for sure and have done before, Salt Rock Cave is one of them. This Salt Rock Cave, Admiral's Lair, has a long history as a gold mining site. So, inside we have several ogres - lair guards who have made this cave their home. It's often the case in WoW that ogres have some pretty crazy loot tables, and these guys, well, are no exception.

In fact, I think they are the reason for this saying, because their loot tables are truly insane. Historically , a lot of the farms and items we hunt in Gold Bound, in relation to a specific mob transmog, are usually one or two unique rare items, but here we are hunting all of their green BOE loot. In the Eastern Kingdoms, most basic green BOE items dropped by mobs typically cost between 50 and 700 gold, which is below the minimum selling price for our current transmog inventory. For us, such a transmog is practically garbage that can only be handed over to a merchant. But here in the Salt Cave, prices for BOE greens can range from 2,000 to over 100,000 gold for the most valuable specimens. So we better start farming.

The route in this cave is quite simple, like in many caves of the Horde's starting zones in Kalimdor, so we can just run in circles, because the ogres here constantly instantly respawn. There are a few places where you have to use grappling hooks or parkour to get through, but overall it's not too difficult. Back to the loot tables: one of the best sets of green BOEs to knock out is the one that gave the cave its name—the Saltstone set . This is one of those classic plate transmog sets, like the Jade or Glorious set, whose value lies in both rarity and appearance. And, to be honest, especially in the way it looks on female character models. Prices for items from this set range from 2,000 to over 100,000 gold for the rarest pieces, such as the nagrinits, with the average cost of an item being between 20,000 and 50,000 gold. These are quite rare items, but even getting a few of these items is a huge bonus for a transmog's inventory.

Not bad. While we are farming the Salt Stone set here, you can get many other quite valuable green BOEs. So overall, these are extremely valuable finds. And, as I said, the plus is that the mobs here have a forced instant respawn. So as long as we run and kill them, the mobs will continue to appear. This place used to be a hot spot for hyperspawning group farms, where five druids or any other class would run around, getting insane kills and tons of transmogrification items. Today, due to the anti- hyperspawn mechanic, we are somewhat limited in our options. After the first clearing of the cave and killing one ogre of each type, mechanics are activated that reduce the gold yield from 30–40 silver per kill to three or four, and also block the drop of green items, in particular the "Salt Stone" set, which is not very good for farming. But, to be honest, for us at Golden Needles, this is n't the worst option, as it increases the rarity of items and prevents bots or groups from driving down prices by flooding the market with hundreds of pieces of the Salt Stone set. So for us, this is quite acceptable: you can drop in here, completely clear the location, try your luck, and then move on to other places to farm. I think this will be a great part of the overall farm in the zone as you accumulate tokens. By the way, about other places for farming, it is worth discussing the main feature.

Or, more precisely, the dungeons in this area —the Thornmane Mounds. Before we go there, you may ask, "Are n't the Kurgans in the Steppes?" In the classic version of the game—of course, yes. But in the retail version and after Cataclysm, it's purely a Thousand Needles dungeon . It is accessible beyond the Big Lift, this climb next to Dark Cloud Peak. We just need to go up, go through the maze, and enter the dungeon. But this entire pre-dungeon area of ​​the Mounds belongs entirely to the Thousand Needles location, and as far as I can see, the Mounds are not accessible from the Steppes in the retail version of the game. However, the Needlemane Labyrinth is still a full-fledged Steppes dungeon, as is the Caves of Tears. So these will have to wait. After all, it's not bad to have three dungeons spread between two zones. And we are heading to Kurgany, travelers.

The presence of this dungeon in Thousand Needles can turn the zone from a B-level to almost S-plus for gold farming. Let me explain. The dungeon route is very simple. It is actually linear, from point to point. Also, there is a convenient exit after the final boss, so you don't have to go back to get out. As for gold in the dungeon, there are several different sources of income. First of all, RFD has the highest number of chests of any dungeon we've opened so far. There are about eight to ten chest spawn points in the dungeon. In most playthroughs, we manage to collect between three and six. Not a bad start. The chest loot tables are pretty standard for classic dungeons and, to be honest, very similar to Uldaman.

One of the most valuable recipes we'll be looking for is the Rich Purple Silk Shirt pattern—an item worth over a million gold if we're lucky enough to obtain it. Again , the significant increase in the value of this item is due to its addition to the achievement for creating things. If you want to get achievement points, you'll either have to knock out the recipe yourself or buy it from a goblin . This item slipped away from us in Uldaman, which we spent over 25 hours farming, but here, in this zone, we will have a much better chance of finding it in chests . Additionally, chests drop a wide range of world-wide items: epic, rare, or unique items like the Broken Blade of Heroes. They also provide a steady stream of trade goods, such as leather and gems, so we want to collect as many of them as possible.

Chest spawn locations: In the first area of ​​the spider cave, one of the chests may appear here. If it appears, you must first catch the spider on the ceiling, otherwise it will jump down and interrupt the process of opening the chest. Further, a little deeper into the dungeon, there is a room with four niches. Each of these niches can contain a chest , and the last one can contain two, so we always check these niches. Then, in the final stage of the dungeon, where we spiral up to the final two bosses, almost every hut along the way may have a chest, so we check them all. Regarding the Rogue specialization, I don't play through the "Thug" in this dungeon, so I don't have a talent for finding treasure. Instead, I use the Elimination specialization because of the AoE damage from Shuriken Storm, which makes it much easier to kill enemies on the move. In addition, it gives a slight acceleration after destroying a group of mobs. But this means that we have to search for chests manually in each location, rather than relying on the mini- map. But what else is in this dungeon?

Well, travelers, here is one extremely important improvement for your character. Returning to the alcove, we see what looks like the remains of an echinoderm, and above it is a small bag, Henry's bag. This is Henry Stern from the classic version of the dungeon, and during every run, this bag hangs here. And during the first run, when you take her, she gives you a reagent bag. Yes. So, we've officially unlocked our first character reagent bag, and we can add it to our four deep-sea bags to get an additional 10 item slots . This is simply incredible. The reagent bag is personal, at least when you first get it, but we can still pick it up every time, and it's actually worth it because it always has a recipe for goldenrod tea, a recipe for a good worth about 3,000. And since it's here every run, I'll be collecting five to ten of these recipes to gradually sell over the next few months. Always a nice find.

This dungeon is already proving to be quite interesting. Now about the loot tables. Unlike some of our previous transmog farming dungeons where we hunted for super items and specific blue items (BOEs). Here in RFD, we have many of the same drop rates as in the Salt Cave, which means that it is the green items here that can be worth quite a bit of gold. We have the Salt Stone set, of course, but also many other green transmogrification items worth between 5k and 40k gold. There are also some blue BOEs that drop here and can be worth anywhere from 100k to 400k gold, but they're not quite the super items we hunted in Uldaman. However, with green drops, the average value of a single dungeon run is around 20,000 gold.

Of course, this is the market value of a transmog, calculated based on a large sample, so the actual gold income per run may vary. Additionally, since this is the market value of the transmog, the actual profit from these items may be lower or it may take a long time to sell them. But it's still a top- tier dungeon if you want to get into transmog and want to fill your first 200–400 cells with valuable items. So, that's all. Is n't that right? Well, not exactly. This dungeon is actually also a place for stable farming. Listen to me. For these runs, I use herbalism and dungeon enchantment. In fact, two herbs appear quite often here: Goldenthorn and Gravemoss, which are currently the two most valuable herbs in Classic WoW. So as I move on , I track down the herbs and collect them all. In an hour of farming here, where I manage to make about nine runs, I collect over 26 Golden Spikes and 48 Grave Moss.

Although their prices range from 18 to 28 gold, the average is around 1,600 gold per hour on herbs alone. Not bad at all . Additionally, through enchantment, we can recycle items and loot that we don't intend to use or sell. Due to the way item levels are scaled, the green stuff here is about 40 levels higher than the blue stuff that drops from bosses. Therefore, it is more profitable to sell green items to a merchant than to dispose of them. The ones I don't want to auction, I just sell to a dealer. Due to this, the average amount of " pure" gold from sales and collection is about 1,000 gold per hour. Even though we sell green items, we still have blue items that become personal when selected. It is more profitable to spray them for a chance to get large eternal essences than to sell them to a merchant, as the buyback prices for these items are quite low.

Spraying blue stuff during an average hour of farming yields us around 35 essences, each of which currently costs 18 gold. That's another 630 gold. So, all this gives a stable income of 3200 gold per hour, which in itself is not impressive, but if you consider that the main goal is transmog, and we get over 180,000 gold of market value of transmog every hour. This stable gold becomes a nice bonus. We will spend a few more hours here at the farm and report on our most valuable finds. For now, it's worth looking at a more stable source of income. I don't want to quit herbalism right now because we're going to be farming a lot more in RFD. For the same reason, I also don't want to give up on casting spells just yet. So I think the double collection will have to be postponed. Besides, there aren't many places around to mine ore. In fact, most of the ore deposits are located on the borders, and the borders between Thousand Needles, Tanaris, and Feralas are quite dangerous. So I don't want to waste a lot of time flying in these questionable places.

For now, let's stick to herbalism. I think there might be an interesting opportunity here. The kelp is suffocating because it is abundant under the surface of the water on the former bottom of the zone. Now it's relatively cheap, about five gold coins apiece, but about six months ago the price reached 20-30 gold coins. So I think we should try to farm it. The only downside is that it's underwater, and while we have a few underwater means of transportation, like the New Moon Fair Ramp or the Poseidon's Reins from Vaish'ir, we can't breathe underwater. I would have to surface every minute or two to replenish my air supply. To make this a little more efficient, we'd better open up the ability to breathe underwater. Unfortunately, we can't do this the traditional way through quests in this area, because for the Alliance they start in Feralas, and it's not open for us yet.

Luckily, I know another way, because today is Sunday, and the fishing tournament in Stranglethorn Valley is about to begin. And we're lucky that we've already opened and received our token in Stranglethorn Vale, so we can pop in there for a few useful upgrades. To start, we need to win the tournament by catching 40 delicious fish. I'm lucky because no one has won yet, and I'm just returning to Pirate's Cove. Here we are. There are several awards here. We already got the Arcanite Fishing Rod, but today I need the Master Fisherman's Hook—an accessory that turns you into a fish and allows you to breathe underwater. Ideally. So, having received our new accessory, let's return to the zone and test our farm. It seems that in fish form we move slower than underwater vehicles, and we can't fight underwater. However, the good thing is that we can still collect herbs in the shape of fish. If we mount a beast, the fish shape will not disappear. We can safely swim on our vehicles and breathe underwater. Perfectly. Time to start farming. As for algae, there are a huge number of them down here. I don't have a specific route , but in general I try to make as many circles as possible around this area. As you can see, apart from the algae, there's really nothing special going on here. Due to the long distances, we only collect about 246 algae per hour. At current market prices, this works out to 1,230 gold per hour. Not very impressive, but worth keeping in mind, because if the price of suffocating algae jumps back to 30 gold, this will instantly turn into a farm with an income of 7,300 gold per hour. And, as far as I know, this is probably the best place to collect suffocating algae in terms of production volume.

But I don't want to spend too much time here, at least not at these prices. However, while we're here, it's worth checking out the underwater mobs. There are several turtles here, which is quite interesting, maybe it's worth making a turtle farm here. Although we don't have the skinning skills right now, so I'd rather leave them alone. Plus, there's South Sea Treasure Hunters. As it turns out, they have a pretty good list of possible loot. The same things drop as in the entire area, for example, salt rock. The downside is that they are far apart and underwater, so the kill rate here is horribly low. Well, of course, they still have epic items on their loot list that drop all over the world. Oh, look at this. We just knocked out the Staff of Jordan. This is our first epic item in the world on the character Goldie.

That is, we have already found blue things that become personal when worn, but there have been no epic ones yet. And we've been playing for over 45 days. Besides, the Rod of Jordan is a pretty good thing. Of course, there are better options, like the Skullfire Shield. But hey, these guys are proving their worth. Even if a mob doesn't look the best on paper, we always have a chance of dropping epic loot. So far, Thousand Needles is living up to expectations. But that's probably all there is to see underwater. Although, in fact, there are a few rare enemies here. The most notable of these is Krikks, who drops a good weapon for transmogrification: the Silithid Ripper. This is a one-handed weapon with a market value of over 100,000 gold, but that's just the market price. Given the data across all servers and recent sales, it will likely go for significantly less, but it's worth checking.

So, I think we're done with the underwater part of this zone . So let's head back to shore for our next gold farm. Here, on the Clefthoof Heights in the northeastern part of the zone, there is a centaur camp— Camp Galak. And here we are only interested in one type of mob and one item: Galak the Torturer, these are centaurs in purple-blue armor. And the prey we're hunting is none other than the Marauder's Heavy Scimitar, a classic unique item that only drops from them. This item is insanely valuable, over 230,000 gold, and auction prices usually exceed 400,000. Currently, the cheapest lot on all North American servers costs over 100 thousand. The drop rate is unknown for certain, as the item was unavailable for several expansions, skewing Wowhead's statistics, but it is listed at 0.02%, or nine out of 50,000 kills. So, I'll do a few kills of these mobs, but I don't expect to get it without spending a huge amount of time. Well, in less than 200 kills, in about an hour and a half to two hours of farming, we knocked out this sword. Travelers, you won't believe it, but it's true. I don't know if I'm incredibly lucky or if Wowhead's drop tables are completely inaccurate . I'm guessing both, and the drop chance is closer to 0.2%, but hey, we're already getting crazy loot in this area, and we haven't even sorted out the loot from RFD yet. I think I can postpone this farming for now, although there is another rare mob nearby, in the valley to the north —the Cancer. It doesn't have any special unique items, but overall it's pretty good loot, the same goes for another rare mob in the east—Skyshadow.

The drop is not bad, but nothing too valuable to mention. But while you're farming looters, it's definitely worth killing rare mobs if they appear. Regarding farming strategy: since it's close to Southsea Holdfast and Saltstone Cave, to avoid the anti-hyperspawn mechanic, I would do one lap around the cave and then clear all the Maulers, which took 5-6 minutes, before returning to the cave. And so on in a circle. I don't know if the scimitar and maulers are affected by the open world loot bugs, but that's how I farmed them and ended up getting them in less than 200 kills, so it definitely didn't hurt. Considering the farming in this area, we have three extremely profitable places for transmog and one very weak one for stable income.

We'd better try to find a really stable place to farm. While flying through the area, I discovered something very interesting. So, look at this. Yes, this is probably the highest concentration of turtles in the game. This island is home to stranded Sparkle Shell turtles. These turtles must have climbed out here, onto this ledge, during the flood and cataclysm, and we can make money from it. Although, to be fair , not all the turtles in this area made it to these places. Unfortunately, you can't rob the dead in the water , otherwise we would definitely visit there from time to time . But there are two main ledges here where turtles gather. One of them is in the far east of the zone, and the other is right here, much closer to the center and the entrance to the dungeon.

Each of these ledges has about 15-18 turtles in a relatively small area. And if the Swamp of Sorrows taught me anything , it's that turtle farming can be more profitable than expected. These guys can be robbed, of course, so I'll have to give up on casting enchantments for a while to get my skinning up to 280, because then we can get everything they have to offer. When that's done, you can start removing the skins. They belong to the category of heavy and thick leather. Currently, heavy leather costs between five and eight gold pieces, and thick leather costs between eight and 12 gold pieces. But these prices fluctuate quite a bit depending on the market, so they may change. And these are just the basic skins.

Since it is a heavy leather, we can also get heavy rawhide. This is definitely a valuable item, although prices have dropped a bit, but are still hovering around 60-100 gold. Also , since they are turtles, we can also get turtle scales when skinning them. And most importantly, it's not a replacement for skins. We get scales in addition to regular skin. These things can also vary greatly in price. I used to sell some of them for more than 20 gold in the Swamp of Sorrows, but now the market has stabilized at six to eight gold. Not bad. It's still a good income, but the loot doesn't end there, because these are just materials that can be removed from the skin. Turtles have several other valuable trade items on their prey list. Of course, the classic mollusk with a large mouth. These things have been a bit of a mystery throughout my gold-hunting journey. They sell well themselves, but they can also be opened in the hope of finding a golden pearl. The current price of clams ranges from 12 to 20 gold depending on the day of the week. But a golden pearl—well, it costs a little over 500 gold pieces apiece.

So, the age-old question arises: should we open clams for a chance to find a pearl, or sell them as is? I think this can be answered with another question. Would you like to buy lottery tickets or sell them? Because now, at current prices, the expected cost of opening shellfish will result in us losing about 50% of their value on average. Because when I was in the Scorched Lands, I tested it by opening a thousand things. Not to mention that I've opened a few hundred more clams before this, and my current gold pearl drop rate is around 2%. So, unless the value of 50 clams is less than the price of one pearl—in which case 50 clams are worth about 1,000 gold— we're better off just selling the clams as is. Of course, this is just the probability of falling out. Of course, you can take a chance and open 10 clams and get 10 pearls, but we take enough risks during our dungeon crawls, so I'll just sell these. In addition, you can get meat from turtles, which costs 4.5 gold per piece. These guys have a bunch of different trade goods worth anywhere from 4 to 20 gold each, so we farm them.

As for farming these mobs, unfortunately there is no hyperspawning on turtle islands. We have to run between two islands, but we kill them much faster than they can respawn, so we either have to clear both islands and wait 4 minutes—which, to be honest, is not bad when editing a video—or find something else to do in that time, which I think is best: clear the two large islands and then jump into the Saltstone Cave to do one round of the ogres. This diversifies loot, avoids the hyperspawning mechanic in the cave, and provides a good balance between trade goods and transmog. But for testing, I want to try a full farm on skinning . So to get hourly figures I'll just work a few smaller turtle camps around the area. There are also several groups of two or three individuals left alone.

Also, to make sure everything is respawning, grab some high-density cloud snakes found on the tops of the spires. The one closer to the first island usually has the most turtles, so I'll choose that one. They don't drop as good loot as clams, turtle meat, or scales, but they still yield heavy and thick hide. So, this helps to increase your profit in gold per hour, instead of just waiting for turtles. After testing, what is the real profit in gold per hour we get from the goods? Well, I got 402 units of pure gold through merchant trash, which is pretty good. We then got 89 clams, 180 heavy leather, 12 heavy hides, 180 thick leather, and 284 turtle scales, which at current prices is just over 8,000 gold per hour. Not bad at all. And, to be honest , it's definitely worth checking the prices, because who knows, in a few months they might go back to their old rates, and it'll be around 14,000 gold per hour. Not to mention that I missed out on extra items during testing.

We actually avoid the anti-hyperspawn mechanic , so we keep getting green and blue items. I got a blue BoE item, swamp walker boots, which aren't worth much, plus a few low-cost green transmogrification items. I won't count them towards my gold per hour figure, but it's a nice little bonus. So, in Thousand Needles, we now have several top-notch transmogrification farms, plus a steady income of 8,000 gold per hour. Not to mention the reagent bag. I would say this makes Thousand Needles a top tier zone for gold farming and, frankly, a top tier zone for farming in general. So while we're on this wave, let's do our raid sweeps for the week. This week they are sponsored by Gold Capped. This is a powerful resource for gold farming with guides and tools, as well as a premium Discord server for communicating with other players and asking questions to the guide authors. I have been working with them since the beginning of the Gold Bound project, and honestly, the biggest advantage here is the operations and TSM groups to start working with resale or general display of goods . Plus their real-time updated farm search, which ranks guides by gold per hour based on auction data for EU and NA.

Quick, pause to kill Onyxia, which unfortunately was not lucky. But if you want to try Gold Capped, use my code Pathaleerix10 at checkout to get 10% off guides or subscriptions. Now that I've finished the raids, I'll pop over here to Arat for some rare creatures for the front. We can only kill these guys for loot once every three or four weeks, so we might as well take this chance. We're still mostly looking for mounts and transmogs for Goldie, but you can also sell pets, so let's see what we can get. Oh, there it is. Withered Bark Wing. And our first flying vehicle that isn't a Golden Griffin. Honestly, it looks pretty good, so I'll take it. So, last but not least —Fiery Bosom . We are now at the 42nd event. Can we finally grab the last Windseeker tether for the Thunder Lute, the Blessed Blade of the Windseeker?

No. What about the Nightshadow Slayer Chestpiece, an item with a supposedly 20%+ drop chance, and the final piece we're missing for the set? Oh, he fell out. Well, that means one thing. That's all. The new transmog is unlocked, and dare I say, we're looking pretty good. I also switched to Maladath and Chromatically Tempered Swords, which , to be fair , pair quite well with the Withered Bark Wing. Perfectly. But while we were farming and working in this area, I had already recorded 100 runs in RFD. I sent all the dropped items to my secret character for transmog in Thousand Needles. So everything on this character is collected in this area. Let's see what the auction looks like. So, we have 333 items on display with a total value of over 1.9 million gold.

Some madness. Some of this dropped as regular items in the zone and in the Salt Cave, so it's not all from RFD, but still, we made an insane amount of gold in this zone. Let me show you some of the most valuable finds . First, and most importantly, is the Broken Blade of Heroes. It's something like a blacksmithing recipe, but single- use, and its cost is between 40,000 and 1 million gold. I've listed it at a relatively aggressive price— around 125,000 gold— but it can also be reforged into a blade using a classic blacksmith. The blade has similar competition and auction prices. So I decided to see if I could sell the broken blade quickly before I tried to reforge it at an alto- craftsman. We also picked up a bunch of items from the salt kit.

Almost everything except the blades and maybe the bracers, to be honest, and they are, to be fair , the most expensive parts. We also have a few miscellaneous BOE items from dungeons, like the Ice Shard from RFD. Of course, we're also trying to sell the Marauder's armor set quickly while we're in this area. As well as " Fists of Straw Storm", " Boots of Thorns" and "Boots of Enlightenment". Additionally, RFD literally generates an insane amount of medium-value green items. Things range from two to 30,000 gold. I mean, just look at all these lots. I don't list more than two at a time to save on auction commission, but we've clearly gotten carried away here. So, it's fair to say that we've collected a bunch of valuable stuff in this area, but how quickly can we sell it?

So here I am farming turtles in the Salt Cave, still looking for the elusive leg chains of course, but I have to say, I didn't expect Thousand Needles to become my favorite gold-earning zone. There's incredible value here thanks to zone drops and rare items, not to mention dungeons and turtles. Well, there's nothing better than a turtle farm . So I'm relisting lots, checking competitors' prices, and trying to get things moving . Let's move on to the trade goods auction and see how much we made this week for Goldie. Who knows? Maybe we already have enough to unlock a new zone. First, we earned gold, mostly from races in RFD, and the token costs 267,000 gold. Let's look at our results. There are 170 lots of goods for trade, and even some "fire water " over the last couple of days. Using the New Moon Fair each time after the cooldown ended brought 2.3k gold.
Not bad. And, of course , some herbs and skins. Let's summarize everything and see the overall result of trading. Honestly, I spent a lot more time on transmog than I did on stable gold.

Okay. So, we have a little over 60,000 gold, about 47,000 of which are from trade goods, which seems a bit low, but, hey, it happens. It seems that competitors have appeared on the turtle farm and are undercutting prices. I will check prices more often and relist lots, hoping to sell everything faster. Now let's check the characters for transmog. Let's start with the accumulated stock. It seems like we sold a lot of cheaper transmog items, which makes sense. This week was " Style Test," so the cheaper items are probably being snapped up. Oh, well, that's nice. We sold the skull plate bracers for 100,000 gold. This is the same blue item we got in Uldaman. And, in my opinion , that's a pretty good price for them.

Also Bullet of Deception. I think this week with transmog could be a good one. So, let's take all of this and look at the result. 133,000 gold. Not a bad week for a character with accumulations. What about the viola in Thousand Needles? There I exhibited lots a little more aggressively. Well, apparently not everything always sells. As it is, so it is, and transmog is a long game. So we need to continue to develop this viola, which seems to be already bearing fruit. So, together with Goldie, we have 196,000 gold, and only about 60,000 short of a token. But, to be fair, we still have 20,000 gold in goods waiting to be sold, and a great new farm. Not to mention the pile of transmog that still needs to be sold. So we can get back to business sooner than expected. Until then , go with honor , my friend.

paragraphs.text: Greetings travelers and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where we're farming our way through Azeroth one zone at a time. In each new zone we explore, uncover some of the best and some of the worst gold farms until we've earned enough gold to buy a WoW token. Then, and only then, can we spin the randomizer for a new zone. In last episode, we entered into Thousand Needles, blitzed through some of the best transmog and dungeon farms in the series so far, the likes of the Saltstone Cave and Razorfen Downs. But, transmog sales were kind of slow and we left off with a mailbox clear shooting us just under 200,000 gold, which isn't quite enough because the WoW token has been hovering around 260,000 gold lately. I have had a few extra days to keep items listed, try to do some undercuts, and even skin a few more turtles. Let's go ahead and see where things are sitting at at the moment because who knows, we could have a new zone spin sooner than expected.

Well, not bad. A few trade goods and some sales from the backlog transmog alt, but really not too much here. The big movers are definitely the turtle scales and clams, so the turtle farm is coming in clutch. Let's get this all loaded up and see exactly where we're sitting. Okay, okay, so 214,000 gold out of 261,000 for the token. Well, we better get back to farming. And honestly, the best consistent farm I've found so far in the zone is looking to be the turtle skinning farm. So, while I plug away on that, let me show you a few other notable farms and items in the zone because I have had a chance to poke around a little bit more in the zone.

First and foremost, check out this guy, Mad Megus Turth, who is up at Turth's haunt here over in the far east of the zone. He hangs around the blue casting circle and once we take him out, we actually get what is either a ghost of his past or someone whose enchantments are no longer working on, aka a vendor, who just so happens to sell Ancona chickens, a battle pet. Now, the base version of this pet here only sells for about 50 to 100 gold, but the purchase price is only one gold. So, really not a bad markup. Plus, if we learn the chicken into our battle pet log and then put it into a cage, we do get the caged version, which is a different auction house listing and actually has a market value closer to about 200 to 800 gold.

Not a bad little zone vendor to stop by at. But really, we aren't going to make up the 45,000 gold for the next WoW token by selling chickens. At least not today. Although, we may get there on turtles. And in between laps of the turtle islands, which we're pretty much just repeatedly skinning on here at this point, I also like to pop up into the Saltstone Cave for a chance at some of the rare drops. A quick run through gives us a little extra juice to our consistent gold farms here and a chance at some rare drops. So, while we get after some more turtle and Saltstone Cave farming, let me tell you about the sponsor of today's episode because there is some awesome new IP and champions coming to the game. After defeating the Wicked Witch of the West, Dorothy Gale and her dog Toto, alongside her friends the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion have some new adventures, The Echoes of Oz. So, for a limited time, you can claim the brand new legendary champion Dorothy Gale for free by logging in for seven consecutive days during the Dorothy Gale Chase. Plus, if you keep logging in for another seven days, you can earn extra gear upgrades for Dorothy and take on a Zilta the Wicked as the event dungeon boss in the limited time event dungeon to earn Chronophage gear and other valuable rewards. So, with the current promos, it's a great time to test out Raid: Shadow Legends and I've been enjoying the new champions that keep coming out test. But also the ease of just jumping into the game and getting going. And speaking of jumping into the game, if you haven't started playing yet, new players can get some awesome sign-up bonuses up through my link for free.

Like Narma the Returned, a legendary champion. She's a powerful one with poison explosion damage and healing for sustain. Plus, you can also get another free legendary champion of your choice using any of the following promo codes: Alice the Wanderer with code get Alice, Cheshire Cat code Kitty Cut, Peela the Victor, Super Victory, and Grand Oak Padraig, code Wrath. I would recommend Peelops the Victor as a tank champion to contest out and build some teams around. Plus, of course, if you log in for seven consecutive days, you'll get the legendary champion Dorothy for free. And if you reach level 15, you'll get the champion Kanoru, who excels at debuffing enemies. So, big thank you to Raid for sponsoring today's episode, and let's get back to the gold.

With all the excitement though, and new drops, we may as well take a look at the auction house and the mailbox to see if we have sold enough to make up the difference. But as you can see here, as I've been farming away, the WoW token price has actually shot up to about 272,000 gold, which I can't really act surprised here because patch 12.1 is coming out right away, the Curse of Ulatek, and a lot of people are probably returning to the game for the new zone, dungeon, and raid, and maybe buying WoW tokens to pay for that sub. So, as you can see, we did get a few extra sales on the transmog alts. Nothing massive, but a few smaller pieces moving. On top of that, a whole bunch of turtle scales, clam meat, and leather is showing up in the mailbox. So, let's go ahead and get this all loaded up to see if we're spinning for a new zone. Well, not quite. We are up to 253,000 gold though, about 19k short. But really, that's just a few more hours of turtles.

So, let's keep it rolling. Now that I think of it though, there are a few other little things in the zone that could bring in some more gold, like this rare, Iron Eye, a basilisk. Much like a few other mobs in the zone, he has a pretty notable weapon drop on his loot table, the Blade of the Basilisk. This one-handed sword has a market value of about 30,000 gold, so it is definitely worth tagging. That being said, he is one of the more regularly camped rares in the zone, so it can be a bit harder to get consistent tags on him, especially since we're usually down in the waters going after the turtle spawns. Speaking of zones though, and since we're in the final leg of farming for the WoW token, let's Let's about what zones we can actually roll for.

First up, and back over to Eastern Kingdoms, we have our southernmost zone that hasn't been hit yet, Deadwind Pass. This zone has missed 14 consecutive zone spins, so I think it might be time. Then further north, we do have the Twilight Highlands, a Cataclysm zone with a few raids and material farms. Continuing past Arathi Highlands, we do have Hillsbrad Foothills, a classic mid-level questing hub and home to the Alterac Mountains and Alterac Valley for that matter. And the last Eastern Kingdoms zone, the Hinterlands, which is basically the mother lode of archaeology dig sites, home to three of them at the moment. All good options. Then back over here on Kalimdor, we of course have the Barrens, a foothold into the Horde questing zones. Then recently put onto the zone spin options thanks to Thousand Needles, we also have Feralas, home to Dire Maul and some trade good farms. And last but not least, Tanaris, a massive zone with the Caverns of Time, Zul'Farrak, and not to mention the pathway to other massive gold per hour zones. So seven options total, and honestly, all of them would be great. Back to the token grind, and unfortunately, it does seem like the WoW token spike from the retail patch is moving the target about as fast as I can make gold right now, which we're up to 261,000 gold was where the token was at just a few days ago, but now the token is sitting squarely at 280,000 gold. So it's back to a few more hours of turtles, and honestly, I'm looking forward to a new zone with the options we have.

All right. Another mailbox clear, and I think we actually have it right now unless we have a crazy spike in the token. Luckily overnight the token price did drop, and we also sold a few more of our materials. And with that, a new WoW token in the bags. I did scoop this one up relatively quickly before the token spiked again, but travelers, that does mean we can spin for a new zone straight away. First things first though, we have some cluttered bags and and 3,300 gold extra to spare, saving up for the 500,000 gold needed for the next tab. And then clearing up the bags and get ready to spin. So, travelers, if you're enjoying the series so far, then consider subscribing to not miss future episodes and zones. But for now, well, let's see where we're going today.

Oh, the Hinterlands, the archaeology haven. Well, let's go. For this one, the best path that we have, and well, the only path we have into the Hinterlands is actually through a Raff Basin. There's a tunnel here that heads straight up into Hinterlands. So, let's go on in. There we go. A brand new zone to explore, and might I say, a nice change of scenery. It's looking somewhere between Elwynn Forest and Grizzly Hills, fine by me. So, this zone is actually a little bit of a smaller one compared to some of our recent unlocks, but we do have a few key areas, like the dwarf stronghold of Aerie Peak, the forested roads, home to owlkin and wolves, the North Quel'Thalas Lodge, a high elf stronghold, plus the Glen of Seradane. Then down to the south, we have a variety of troll ruins, like the Altar of Zul, Jintha'Alor, Revantusk Village, and of course, over on the shore, turtles. Will the turtle meta return? We'll just have to see. First and foremost, there is one thing on my mind, well, three things actually, the archaeology dig sites. So, let's get digging. Now, archaeology might not normally be that interesting to most retail players, but in a zone locked challenge like Goldbound, it opens up the table to a whole new variety of zone-based luck. Because on each continent, there's always four archaeology dig sites up, meaning, whenever one dig site is completed, it forces one to spawn in one of the other archaeology sites in one of the other zones on the continent. Although, the game doesn't know which zones we have unlocked. So, until we have every single Eastern Kingdom zone available, the dig sites will eventually spawn into locked zones, which is exactly what happened the first day we unlocked archaeology when all of the dig sites pretty much went to Hinterlands. Lucky for us, it means we have three fresh chances to run through this. As far as archaeology goes, we can get some nice upgrades like the Raptor mount, but also for Goldie, archaeology is some of the highest XP per hour that we can get. For example, we've spent almost 5 days played, or 125 hours to get halfway through level 84 so far, but each of the archaeology tablets, which you get about six per dig site, gives us 6,000 XP, at least while we're rested.

It does take us on a wild goose chase all over Eastern Kingdoms, but so far, with the first Hinterlands dig site done, it does take us down to Searing Gorge, and finishing this one up, it sends us back down to Stranglethorn Vale. Finishing up the first Stranglethorn Vale dig site, and uh yeah. So, it spawned in Eastern Plaguelands, which is a squarely locked zone, which means we're down to two active dig sites, and we'll have to see how far we can get before those two are also locked into other zones. On to the next one in Hinterlands here, and well, dinged up lady five. Not bad on the XP at all. Based on the number of zones, I think each time we finish a dig site, there's about a one in three chance that the site goes to a locked zone. And with that in mind, travelers, we ended up going on a generational run of dig sites. They just kept dropping in unlocked zones, and we kept grabbing them. And when I say generational, I mean it. About 20 dig sites over two straight hours. We went to all the way from level 85 to 86 in this one insane run of archaeology. Of course, all good things like this come to an end, and the last one respawned up north, but hey, I can't complain because we burned through all of our rested XP, and we're already three bars into level 86, not to mention level 339 for archaeology. Seriously not too shabby, but this is gold bound after all and we have a brand new token to chase to hopefully spin for a new zone and there was gold. Now each dig site has one kind of artifact. In our current Eastern Kingdom zones, we can get fossil, troll, or dwarf artifacts.

Usually we get our own soul bound artifacts, but sometimes we get a rare tradeable version. These can be used artifact crafts for troll or dwarf fragments, but for us, we can also sell them on the auction house to other players to use in their crafts. And over the two hours of farming, I got seven troll fragments worth about 300 to 500 gold each. On top of that, two dwarf runes worth 200 to 400 gold each. So about 3.1 thousand gold for the tradeable fragments, but that's not all because in the end, I actually procced a rare troll archaeology craft. It takes a hundred of our troll fragments to craft and it gives us the voodoo figurine, which we can learn, promptly put into a cage, and then sell on the auction house for upwards of 9,000 gold. Yep. So all in all, with vendor items included, we pulled in about 12,200 gold for two hours of archaeology, working out to about 6,100 gold per hour. A good chunk of that was the pet, which very well may just be dumb luck and the actual gold per hour might be a lot lower, but hey, at least for our sample size here, we'll call that some good gold per hour from archaeology. On top of the archaeology loot though, since we were covering such large distances across the whole continent, I did have track treasure on. I actually found quite a few treasure chests. From the chests in Hinterlands, which just so happened to have a lot of archaeology sites and a lot of chests, I got a few things. First up, the Archaic Defender, an absolute gem of a transmog find and one that we shouldn't have trouble selling over the next couple weeks or months because it has both a solid market value of about 60,000 gold but also a super clean appearance.

And then from the assorted chest that I saw while flying between dig sites, I pulled in three more blues. The Twisted Chanter's Staff, about 3 to 4,000 gold. The Shield of Thorson, about 6 to 12,000 gold. And the Drake Wind Bands, about 9,000 gold. So all in all, on top of archaeology, we got some pretty insane market value just flying around Eastern Kingdoms. But we're in Hinterlands after all, so let's get after some regular zone farms. There is one that I think we should test out first because we still have skinning leveled up from Thousand Needles and I did happen to see some turtles on the west coast of the Hinterlands here, the Saltwater Snapjaws. These guys are spread across the shores just past the Overlook Cliffs and a few of them are even hanging out in the water. So what do we do? We farm them. As I'm testing it out here, there are two main issues.

First up, they're spread out relatively far and with the turtles that are in the water, they do make it pretty hard to get a really fast respond rate. Without killing all the underwater turtles, it doesn't really feel like they're on a true hyper spawn. And the second downside, well, it's the loot tables. We're still getting turtle meat and the regular skins of heavy leather and medium leather, but unlike our turtles back in Swamp of Sorrows, Blasted Lands, and recently Thousand Needles, these guys don't drop the big clams and when skinned, they don't even give turtle scales. So the total loot table is pretty much cut in half and our kill per hour rates are down quite a bit, which unfortunately doesn't make it the best gold farm. That being said, we're still in the heavy leather band, so we can get lucky and pull in some heavy hide to balance it out. But with my testing here, we're only able to pull in about 2,400 gold per hour, which isn't a crazy amount on its own, but it's still on par with some of our Elwynn Forest rates.

Seeing as we're in a pretty high level zone though, I think the turtle meta may be failing here. So let's get on to some other farms, which we do actually have a few notable vendors in the zone to frequent and try to flip some of their wares. The closest one to our current location on the shore is just up the hills here over in the Stormfeather Outpost with some dwarves. The one that we want in particular, none other than Brannick Ironbelly. He has a ton of white items, which actually have pretty reasonable market values for the plate mail and brigandine sets. Plus, he also has some limited supply greens that we can snag. These ones are in the two to five thousand gold range, so it is definitely worth stopping by Brannick a few times a day to try to pick these up.

Then on to the other vendors. So, if we head up over to the northeast of the Kvaldir Lodge, there's actually a little gnome lookout here. And inside of it, Rupo Zipcoil. He has a few limited supply engineering recipes like the Mithril Mechanical Dragonling. These sell for a few thousand gold in the auction house, but only cost us about 40 silver, which isn't a bad markup. And outside, his business associate, Gidget, can have a few items as well. But, it looks like his stock is sold out at the moment. Now, that isn't all the vendors in the zone, but I might keep another one on the down low for a little bit longer to hopefully choose one of few sales. With that, we do have a marginal farm on the turtles and a few decent little vendor flips to try out.

But, with our archaeology sites all locked away and still no solid consistent farm, things are looking kind of grim in the Hinterlands. So, when in doubt, let's do a gather. I will have to drop my skinning here to go level mining up to about 200 to get the full ranks for the ores here. But, luckily we pretty much have herbalism still maxed out from Thousand Needles, so it doesn't take too long to get to speed and to get testing. The area of the zone is pretty small here in the Hinterlands. Not to mention, there is no Vis a Dormi to swap time phases here to try to reset nodes. So, we are running into a little bit of an herb and ore shortage. It isn't anything too crazy, but it definitely feels like we can loop around the zone faster than the herbs and ores respawn. So, I think down the road in this zone, there may be an optimized route that loops into another zone, like Arathi, just so we have a bigger route to give the nodes more time to spawn. As far as the Hinterlands yield for herbs though, there's quite a big variety. The big one being Goldthorn, a classic high-value herb in the series, but then also a few blindweed spawns. Mostly around the lakes and the troll camps, and this is a minor unlock for the challenge. We haven't really had any blindweed readily available in our previous zones. It's only worth about eight gold each, but it's definitely a good resource to have access to. And there was one more herb that I was hoping to get here, the ghost mushroom.

It's pretty valuable around 33 gold each, and in classic, it used to spawn in the Skullrock caves and then down in the farthest south troll ruins in some more caves. But, I've been through both of those quite a few times on Goldie here, and no ghost mushrooms to be found. Wowhead still has it on there as their spawning in retail, but according to some forums, the ghost mushrooms were removed from Hinterlands during one of the level squishes. So, we'll have to wait for Un'Goro or Feralas to unlock the mushrooms. Oh, well. Then the ores of the zone are pretty straightforward. It's another iron ore band here, so the breadth of it is iron ore, but we can still snag a few gold and silver ore if we get lucky. Not a bad spread. But the results? Well, after an hour of farming, we got a total of eight different types of herbs, which are mostly in the five to 12 gold range, and then 55 of the Goldthorn, which is sitting around 20 to 25 gold right now.

As for ore, we only pulled in 84 iron ore and some really low amounts of gold and silver. So, a really small yield here, and all of this only adds up to a total gold per hour of 3,400. Still better than turtle farming here, but not exactly the juiciest farm to get us out of the zone anytime soon. Here is where the gold stacks up. We only have just under 400 raw gold from the zone so far, but the WoW token has dropped back down to 250k, so a lower target. As for the mailbox, well on Goldie here, we do have a few trade goods moving, but we haven't really gotten stuck into any one farm for too long. And the farms we have done, well they're not too good. So I'll loot this up and see where we fall.

Okay, about 17,000 gold from trade goods, not terrible. How about the transmog? Well, yeah, the entry-level transmog is not moving too well. This won't even cover listing fees. How about the backlog alt though? Definitely better. Quite a few different old items selling here, so let's get this all looted up and see exactly where we fall. 25,000 gold, not bad. Which when we combine that with Goldie's loot, puts us just over 40,000 total gold and about 1/5 of the way to wild token. Which means I better get out there to find some better farms. So until next time, go with honor, friend.

And in between laps around the turtle islands, where we're mostly just skinning for now, I also like to peek into Saltstone Cave in the hope of some rare loot. A quick run adds a little benefit to our steady gold earnings and gives us a chance to get rare items.

So, while we continue to hunt turtles and farm Saltstone Cave, let me tell you about the sponsor of today's episode, as there's a cool new intellectual property coming to the game with Champions. After defeating the Wicked Witch of the West, Dorothy Gale and her dog Toto, along with their friends the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, embark on new adventures—"The Return of Oz." So, for a limited time, you can get the new legendary champion Dorothy Gale for free by logging in for 7 consecutive days during the "Chasing Dorothy" event. Additionally, if you continue to log in for another 7 days, you can earn additional gear upgrades for Dorothy and challenge Azilda the Evil as a boss in a limited- time dungeon to earn Chronophage gear and other valuable rewards. So, with the current promotions, it's a great time to try Raid: Shadow Legends, and I love testing out the new champions that are constantly coming out. And I also like how easy it is to just log in to the game and start playing. And speaking of starting to play: if you have n't started yet, new players can get cool bonuses for signing up through my link, such as Narma the Returned, a legendary champion. She is very powerful, dealing damage with a poison blast and has healing abilities for survival. Additionally, you can get another free Legendary Champion of your choice by using any of the following promo codes. Alice the Wanderer with the code get Alice, Cheshire Cat with the code Kitty Cut, Pylos the Victorious with the code Super Victory, and Padraig the Great Oak with the code wrath. I would recommend Pylos the Conqueror as a tank champion to test and build a team around. And of course, if you log in to the game for 7 days in a row, you'll get the legendary champion Dorothy for free. And if you reach level 15, you will receive the champion Kanoru, who is a master at applying debuffs. A huge thank you to Raid for sponsoring today's episode, and we're back to gold farming. Despite all the hype and new drops, it's worth taking a look at the auction and inbox to see if we managed to sell enough to cover the difference. But as you can see, while I was farming, the price of a WoW token jumped to 272,000 gold. I'm not too surprised, as patch 12.1 "Curse of Ulta'tek" is coming out soon, and many are probably returning to the game for the new zone, dungeon, and raid, perhaps buying tokens to pay for the subscription. So, as you can see, we got a few extra sales through transmogrification characters.

Nothing grand, but a few small things sold. In addition, a pile of turtle scales, shellfish meat, and leather appeared in the mailbox. So let's take all of this away to see if we have enough for a new zone. Well, not exactly. We have 253,000 gold, about 19k short, but that's just a few extra hours of turtle hunting. So let's continue. Although, come to think of it, there are a few other little things in this area that could yield a little more gold, like this rare Iron Eye Basilisk. Like several other mobs in this area, it has a rather valuable weapon on its loot list—the Basilisk Blade. This one-handed sword has a market value of around 30,000 gold, so it's definitely worth adding to your list of targets. However, this is one of the most popular rare mobs in the zone, so it can be difficult to get it , especially considering that we usually hunt turtles in the water. By the way, since we're already at the finish line of token farming, let's talk about what zones we can choose. First, we return to the Eastern Kingdoms, home to our southernmost zone that we haven't visited yet— Deadwind Pass. This zone has missed the pick 14 times in a row , so I think its time has come. Further north we have the Twilight Highlands—a zone from the Cataclysm expansion with several raids and material farms.

Continuing past the Arathi Highlands, we see the Gilsbrad Foothills—a classic hub for mid-level quests, as well as home to the Alterac Mountains and Alterac Valley. And the last zone of the Eastern Kingdoms is the Hinterlands, which is a real treasure trove for archaeology, as there are currently three excavation sites located there. All options are great. Back here in Kalimdor, we have the Steppes, of course, the base for Horde quests, as well as Feralas, which was recently added to the list of zones to choose from thanks to Thousand Needles, home to the Forgotten City and areas for mining goods. And finally, Tanaris is a huge zone with the Caverns of Time, Zul'Farrak, not to mention the path to other locations where you can earn a lot of gold in an hour.

So, we have seven options, and honestly , any of them would be great. Back to token farming, and unfortunately, it looks like the jump in WoW token price due to the patch to the retail version of the game makes the goal as unattainable as how quickly I'm earning gold right now. We have 261,000 gold— that's how much the token was worth a few days ago, but now its price is stubbornly holding at 280,000 gold . So there are still a few more hours of gameplay to go, and honestly, I'm looking forward to the new zone with the options we have. Okay, we're cleaning out the mailbox again, and I think we've already reached our goal, unless the token spikes in price again.

Luckily, the price of the token dropped overnight and we also sold some more of our materials. And with that, the new WoW token is already in our bags. I managed to buy it relatively quickly before the price skyrocketed again, but, travelers, this means we can immediately spin the reel to choose a new zone. But first—we have cluttered bags and about 3,300 gold extra, which we're putting aside for the 500,000 gold needed for the next tab. So, we unpack our bags and get ready to choose. So, travelers, if you like this series, subscribe so you don't miss future episodes and new zones. For now, let's see where we're headed today. Oh, the Hinterlands. A paradise for archaeologists. Come on. For this journey, the best route we have—in fact, the only route to the Inner Lands— is through the Arati Basin. There is a tunnel here that leads directly to the Hinterlands.

So let's go. Well, that's all. A completely new area to explore. And I must say, it's a nice change of scenery. It looks somewhere in the middle between Alvin Forest and Grizzly Hills. I'm fine with it. So, this area is actually a little smaller compared to some of our recent discoveries. But we have a few key areas, like the dwarven stronghold of Airy Peak, the forest roads inhabited by owls, kynes, and wolves, Northern Quel-Dil Lodge—a stronghold of the high elves, as well as Glen Seradine. Further south we have quite a few troll ruins like the Altar of Zul, Jin'ta Alor, the village of Revantusk, and of course the turtles on the coast. Will the turtle meta return ? We will see about that later. First of all, one thing worries me.

Actually, three things. Archaeological excavations. So let's start digging. Archaeology may not be of much interest to most players of the current version, but in a challenge with limited zones like "Gold Bound", it opens the door to new opportunities that depend on luck in the zones. Because on each continent there are always four active archaeological excavation sites. This means that once one excavation site is completed, it forces a new one to appear in one of the other locations on the continent. Although the game doesn't know exactly which zones we've opened. Therefore, until we open up all areas of the Eastern Kingdoms, excavation sites will eventually appear in closed areas. This is exactly what happened on the first day we opened archaeology, and almost all of the excavation sites ended up in the Hinterlands.

Luckily for us, this means we have three new attempts to get through it . Regarding archaeology, we can get some good improvements, for example, the Mount Raptor. But also for Goldie, archaeology is one of the most effective ways to gain experience in an hour. For example, it took us almost five days of game time, or 125 hours, to get halfway through level 84, but each archaeological tablet, of which there are about six in each area, gives us 6,000 experience, at least while we're resting. This has us running around the world of the Eastern Kingdoms, but so far, after the first section in the Hinterlands, we've been sent to the Burning Rift, and after that, back to Stranglethorn Vale. We are finishing the first section in Stranglethorn Valley, and, actually, yes. So, a new location has appeared in the Eastern Plaguelands, which are completely closed, which means we only have two active areas left, and we'll have to see how far we can advance before they too end up in closed areas.

Moving on to the next section in the Hinterlands, and well, congratulations on level 85. With experience, it's not bad at all. Given the number of zones, I think every time we finish a dig site, there's about a one in three chance that the next one will appear in a blocked zone. And with that in mind, travelers, we embarked on an incredible series of excavations that could be called epic. They just kept showing up in open areas, and we kept picking them off. And when I say "incredible," I'm not kidding. About 20 excavation sites in 2 hours straight. We went from level 85 to 86 in this one crazy archaeology run. Of course, all good things must come to an end , and the last place appeared in the north.

But hey, I can't complain, since we've used up all our rest experience and already have three bars at level 86. Not to mention the 339th level of archaeology. Seriously, not bad at all. But it's still a path to gold, and we have a new token to hunt for to hopefully unlock a new zone. And there was gold. So, each excavation site has one type of artifact. In our current Eastern Kingdoms zones, we can get fossils, troll or dwarven artifacts. We usually receive personal artifacts, but sometimes a rare version comes along that can be passed on to others. They can be used to create troll or dwarf fragments, but we can also sell them at auction to other players for their crafting. And in 2 hours of farming, I got seven troll fragments, worth about 300-500 gold each. In addition to this, two dwarven runes, worth 200-400 gold each. So, about 3.1 thousand gold for these fragments, but that's not all. Because in the end, I dropped a rare archaeological troll craft. It requires 100 troll fragments, but we get a voodoo figurine that we can study, immediately place in a cage, and then sell at auction for over 9,000 gold.

Yes. So, overall, including vendor items, we made about 12,200 gold in 2 hours of archaeology, which is about 6,100 gold per hour. A large part of this is a pet peeve, which could very well be just luck, and the real hourly income could be much lower. But hey, at least for our sample, let's call it a good gold per hour figure for archaeology. In addition to archaeological finds, since we were covering such great distances across the continent, I turned on treasure tracking. I really did find quite a few treasure chests. I got something from the chests in the Hinterlands, where there happened to be a lot of archaeological dig sites and chests . First, " Hayek's Magical Defender," a true gem for transmogrification that we'll have no problem selling within a few weeks or months. Because it not only has a solid market value of around 60,000 gold, but also an extremely attractive appearance.

Also, from the chests I saw while flying between excavation sites, I took out three more blue items. " Crooked Spellcaster's Staff", approximately 3-4 thousand gold. " Thornson Shield", approximately 6–12 thousand gold. And " Dragon Wind Bandages", approximately 9 thousand gold. So, overall, in addition to archaeology, we got a crazy market value just by flying through the Eastern Kingdoms. But we're still in the Hinterlands, so let's get down to normal farming in this area. There's one option we should test first, because we still have Thousand Needles skinning up and I've spotted turtles here on the west coast of the Hinterlands— saltwater snappers. These guys are scattered along the shores just beyond the High Cliffs, and some of them are even swimming in the water. So, what do we do? We farm them. While I'm testing here, two main problems arise.

First, they are scattered quite far apart, and because of the turtles in the water, it is very difficult to achieve a quick revival. Unless you kill all the underwater turtles, it seems like they don't respawn as quickly as they should. And the second minus is the loot tables. We still get turtle meat and regular hides— heavy and medium hides—but unlike our turtles in Sorrow Swamp, the Scorched Lands, and recently in Thousand Needles, these don't shed large shells, and when they're skinned, they don't even shed their scales. So, the overall loot table is halved and our kill rates per hour are significantly lower, which unfortunately doesn't make this the best gold farm. That being said , we're still in the heavy leather mining zone, so it's possible to get some heavy hides to balance out the income, but during my testing we were only able to earn around 2,400 gold per hour, which is not much in itself , but still on par with our performance in Elwynn Forest.

Since we are in a fairly high-level area, I think the turtle meta doesn't work here. So, let's move on to other farms, because there are several well-known traders in this area who are worth visiting to try to resell their goods. The closest to our current location on the shore is a little higher up in the hills, at the outpost of Stormfeather, where the dwarves live. The one we need is none other than Branik Iron Belly. He has a bunch of white items that have a pretty good market value for plate and brigand sets. Plus, he has a few limited-edition green items we can grab . These items cost between 2 and 5,000 gold, so it's definitely worth visiting Branik several times a day to try to buy them.

Now let's move on to other merchants. So , if we head northeast from the Lodge of Quel'Danil, we'll see a small dwarven observation post. And inside it is Rupo Zipcoil. It has several limited- quantity engineering recipes, such as the Mithril Mechanical Dragon . They sell at auction for several thousand gold, and they only cost us about 40 silver, which is a good markup. And on the outside, his business partner Gidget may also have a few items, but it seems like he's sold out of everything right now. These aren't all the merchants in this area yet, but I'll probably keep one more a secret for a little longer to hope for good sales. With that said, we have a small turtle farm and some decent resale options, but with our dig sites closed and no steady income, things are looking pretty bleak in the Hinterlands. So, if in doubt, let's gather resources. I'll have to give up skinning to get my mining up to around 200 and get full ranks for the ore here, but luckily we have our herbalism almost maxed out from Thousand Needles, so it won't take long to get into the swing of things and start testing. The Hinterlands area is quite small, not to mention there are no Azidorma to switch time phases for node drops, so we face a slight shortage of herbs and ores. It's not catastrophic, but it definitely feels like we're running around the zone faster than the herbs and ores can spawn, so I think in the future we could optimize the route here that goes into another zone, like Arati, so that we have a longer path and the nodes have more time to spawn. When it comes to herb mining in the Hinterlands, there is quite a lot of variety. Chief among them is Goldenthorn, a classic valuable herb in the series, but there are also several spawn points of Blindgrass, mostly around lakes and troll camps . And this is a small achievement for our challenge.

We didn't have free access to Blindgrass in previous zones before. It only costs about eight gold, but it's definitely a useful resource. There was another herb I was hoping to find here—Ghost Mushroom. It is quite valuable, around thirty gold apiece, and in the classic version it appeared in the Skull Rock caves, as well as in the southernmost troll ruins in a few more caves. But I've already been around both of these places on Gold several times, and I have n't found a single Ghost Mushroom. Wowhead still lists them as appearing in the current version, but according to some forums, Ghost Mushrooms were removed from the Hinterlands during one of the level compressions. So you'll have to wait for Un'Goro or Feralas to discover these mushrooms . Well, okay. The ore deposits in this area are quite simple. This is another iron ore belt, so it's mostly iron here, but we might be lucky enough to extract some gold and silver ore.

Not a bad set. And what about the results? So, after an hour of farming, we got a total of eight different types of herbs, mostly in the 5-12 gold range, and 55 Gold Spikes, which are now worth around 20-25 gold. As for ore, we only mined 84 units of iron ore and very little gold and silver. So, the mining here is quite small, and all of it only yields 3,400 gold per hour. Still better than farming turtles, but not the best way to quickly get out of this zone . This is where the gold accumulates . We only have a little under 400 "pure" gold from this zone, but the price of a WoW token has dropped to 250k, so the target has become closer.

Regarding the mail: we have some trade goods for sale on Gold, but we haven't really stayed in one place for too long. And the farms we did, well, they weren't very successful. So I'll take all of this and look at our summary. Okay, about 17,000 gold from selling goods. Not so bad. What's up with transmog? Well, yes, the Fearless transmog is n't selling very well. This won't even be enough for the placement fee. What about the remaining stock? Definitely better. There are a lot of different old things for sale here, so let's take all the loot and see how much we end up with . 25,000 gold? Not bad. If we add that to Goldie's loot, we'll end up with just over 40,000 gold—that's about 1/5 of the token's value, so I should find better places to farm . So, until next time, go with honor, my friend.
