paragraphs.text: Greetings, travelers, and welcome back to Goldbound, the challenge series where we're unlocking the map of Azeroth by exploring one zone at a time. With each new zone unlocked only once we've earned a WoW token in our unlocked zones, and then we spin randomly. Last episode, we unlocked the Hinterlands, which was a good zone for archaeology. But as far as consistent gold farms, the gold per hour was surprisingly low. After some farming and loot in the mailbox, we're left off with under 50,000 gold to our name and still 200,000 gold to make before we can spin for a new zone. So, travelers, welcome back to the Hinterlands. And let's see if this death zone can provide some profit today, which as far as the hinterlands being a death zone, there's a few reasons why.

First off, well, we haven't really found a consistent gold farm that can truly move the needle here. On top of that, there's actually a few classic hinterlands farms that used to be available, which are just straight up gone now. We already talked about the ghost mushrooms, which have disappeared from the zone entirely, but that isn't where it stops. But more on that later. First up, let's head up to Genta Allore for the troll ruins, which to be fair, there's actually a few gold farms up here. Of course, the spider cave, which used to have ghost mushrooms, doesn't have those anymore. But there's still the spiders themselves inside, which are technically farmable, but they aren't on a hyperspawn, so we will have to wait in between clears of 8 to 12 spiders. On top of the slow clear time, they don't actually really have anything worth farming. They could of course drop some general greens or world drop epics. Technically the trade goods though between the crunchy spider legs which are worth about 45 silver, the large venom sacks about 1 silver, the small spider legs 13 silver, and the thick spider silk which is one of the cheapest spider silk variants at 43 silver. Farming these guys only works out to 63 gold per hour. Yeah, and since we have 200,000 gold left for the token, that would be 3,174 hours or 132 days of straight spider farming. So, spiders, aren't it? But that isn't all we have in genta allore, thankfully, because we do have something else here. Trolls. And in particular, trolls that drop wild vine. Now, this is a super low drop according to Wowhead, around.3%, which is for sure rare, but historically, groups that farm these guys will do a fiveman hyperspawn farm of the entire ruins and get tons of kills per hour. We're of course running a challenge on Goldie here and grouping for open world farms is out of the question, but we can still test it even if we get one every 300 kills. I can kill about 900 trolls per hour solo. And Wildbine is super valuable with a ticket price of 384 gold. Not bad. Most of the trolls do drop this according to Wowhead, but there is one troll archetype here that's a little more interesting. So, while farming Wildbine, we want to make sure to focus on the vile branch hide skinners. These guys can actually drop a rare recipe and maybe the best drop in the whole zone, the pattern for the iron feather breast plate. The recipe itself has an average list price of around 40,000 gold, while the crafted chest piece used with the leather wicking profession goes for about 5,000 gold. So, I will definitely want to farm up at least two of these drops. One just to sell as the recipe because 40,000 gold is pretty much as much as we have right now. and then one to send over to my one crafting alt, golden path, who just so happens to have leather working. So maybe not a death zone after all. Well, not so fast, cuz there's a problem. On testing this, even though Wowhead says the Wildvine is on the drop tables here, my data points otherwise. With thousands of trolls killed, zero wildvine. Looking into the forums, much like the ghost mushroom, when the zone scaling changed here in the hinterlands, the level bracket moved out of the Wild Vine drop range and with it removed yet another gold farm from the hinterlands. Not ideal. So, with that in mind, I'll call the trolls neutral. But that isn't all that Jimthaw Allore has. In addition to the leather working recipe, it has the second best drop in the zone as well. From the rare up in the top in the ruins, Mythreus the Enchanter. Now, this rare is the only one in the zone with a specific item that I feel is worth camping. The other rares are definitely worth killing for low value transmog. Well, this one drops the Chans Imperial Robes, a 20 to 40,000 gold transmog drop. So, we have two notable drops, at least so far in the zone, and we definitely want to camp this one. And since this is really the only mob worth camping in the zone, well, we need something to do in the meantime, which luckily this week's sponsor, Idle Obelisk Miner does just that, which if you're a fan of Goldbound, gold farming, and slow rewarding number go up progression, you're going to want to check this out.

So, this game is actually really all about farming ore, crafting the ore into bars, upgrading your stats, aka your pickaxe, just so you can farm a higher level ore to craft into higher level bars, and well, you get the point, which is very much a gold bound coded. There's also obelisks along the way, which do function as a little bit of a stat check boss, and then drones and bombs to help speed up your gathering. So, while we're camping rares here, we can still be out there farming ore. Oh, yeah. On top of the ore based progression, this game also has no ads, forced or optional, and is built to be completely free to play with limited optional spending if a player wants to.

So, you can get rolling with this without any ads or any costs, which to be honest, in game, there's an awesome sense of continued progression and moving forward. I've been testing and playing it out for a few weeks now, including a few overnight flights, and I really don't feel like I've scratched the surface. It's just a super fun and very much Gold Goblin game, and it's available on all platforms for any mobile device. So, if you'd like to give it a try, and in doing so, support the channel, then click the link in the description and download it today. And there we go. With a little AFK time, we finally got the tag and well, the drop. So, big thank you to Idol Oblisk Miner for sponsoring this video and well, Jam's imperial robes. So, with a few notable drops on the tables, the zone might not seem too bad. The problem is, even with getting these items at their values, we probably won't move them very fast. And if we do, we still need a bit more gold for the token. Of course, we'll list the robes up and try to get some fast sales, but we're going to need something more consistent.

Unfortunately, the time forgotten farms of the hinterlands doesn't end with the wild vine or the ghost mushrooms. Far from it. Because back over at the Skull Rock Cave, the one that used to have ghost mushrooms, we have a few mob types roaming around. The Jade ooze and the green sludge. Historically, both of these mobs used to drop the ooloing bag, a familiar forgotten farm in the series. These are the same bags that used to drop in Swamp of Soros and Wetlands, but in retail, once we're past level 30 to 50 or so, they just stop dropping with mob and item scaling. And well, the hinterlands is no different. So, the ooloing bag, which is valuable because of the battle pet it can contain, the disgusting ooloing, is also lost to the zone. No matter how many of these little oozes we take out, we're not going to get the drop. It's not all bad news, though, because the cave does have some decent ore spawns throughout.

So, it is worth popping in every now and then during mining and herbalism loops to grab the ore. Honestly, I'm sure there's more forgotten farms that I just don't even know about. Another kind of farm that comes to mind is the old repeatable quest in the zone, the troll necklace bounty, which was also removed from the zone. And as far as I know, the Zul rock quest line is also removed from the zone. So, we're working with a little bit of a skeleton farm base here in the Hinterlands. As it stands, we have a few zone vendors, which I still have one up my sleeve, two rare items, and well, dual gathering, which it seems is where a good chunk of the gold is going to have to come from. On that note, I am still doing my dual gathering loops. And on the loops, I'm making sure to check on any rares that are up, plus keeping an eye out for treasure chests in the zone. There's a variety of pretty decently valuable blues that can drop from the chest in the zone, and I want to get as much loot in this zone as possible. For the herbs and ores, though, the rates are generally below 4,000 gold per hour raw. So, for now, I'm actually just stockpiling up with the herbs and ores. I want to get as much as I can while I have the professions. And then later on in the week, I'll drop the gathering professions and switch to some production professions to hopefully mark up our profits. And well, that was kind of my plan to cap out this zone. But travelers, you saw the title of this video, and there is a whole lot more to talk about because right now in live for maybe a day or two after this video comes out, we are in peak BlizzCon season. And generally this wouldn't impact the goldbound challenge, but this time, oh, it does because check this out. The winds of mysterious fortune buff. This actually changes everything.

Sure, the XP boost and rep boost is nice, but what is really wild for a challenge like Goldbound, is that every single mob we kill and quest we do, even in the Hinterlands and our unlocked zones, has a chance to give us a mysterious satchel. Inside the satchel, there's some odds and ends like warbound XP potions, but also gear. Now, this isn't transmog gear. It is all soulbound and actually can't be disenchanted. But there is a full mysterious set to be obtained. The big thing here, though, this gear scales to the level you were when you obtained the satchel. So, while we're running around in these super low-level zones at level 86, wearing item level 30 to 70 gear from our zones, these bags can drop blues and epics with gear item levels of 171 to 178. Pretty much light years better than any gear we can currently obtain in our zones. So, theoretically, we can try to get a full set of current content gear on Goldie while staying in our unlocked zones. So, let's get farming these satchels.

There's a few ways that we can actually get them. First up, there is a bonus each day where the first couple of mobs that we kill just straight up give an epic satchel and the epic satchels always drop the epic gear. On top of that, while killing mobs in the open world or dungeons after that first drop of the day, we can just randomly get blue or epic satchels. Plus, doing quests can give satchels as well. So, let's go test these out. While farming these up though, it is worth noting that this won't be a direct instant gold income for Goldie. It's more of a futurep proofing for later zones where we may have mobs that are scaled way higher. We already had some strange scale like this in Alderman Legacy of Tier where mobs took quite a few hits to kill and well the red ridge spider no feeaster aka the red ridge raid boss which if we do get a full set we're definitely going for revenge. In a challenge like this we generally just don't know what will happen with scaling. It could change wildly with the next expansion and potential stat squishes in the future. So, while a limited time event like this is on, we really need to capitalize on it. With some farming and testing for these satchels under the belt, though, from a satchels per hour perspective, there is a very clear frontr runner. I first tested this out by just killing trolls over and over, and for an hour, we only procked two blue satchels. Not great. I even tried running some old dungeons like Alderman for high kills per hour to try to get some more satchels, but I got none. The real king here is the quests.

Every single quest hand in gives one satchel and about 2,000 XP on top of it. Well, I say every quest, but there are some restrictions. So, repeatable quests, daily quests, or quests where you just go pointtooint and don't actually complete any objectives, those ones don't give a satchel, but regular zone quests do. So, let's lock in and quest through the rest of Hinterlands for some satchels. Okay, so all of the Hinterlands quests are done, and we have about 30 satchels to open here. Quests are definitely the way to go. Looting all these up, we have quite a few of the pieces filled out, but we're still missing out on about four pieces of the mysterious gear. That being said, we are up to 130 item level and over doubling our health pool.

Insane. Luckily, I do have some unfinished quests down in Duskwood. We never actually finish these quests when you're in the zone. So, doing these old quests now, getting another ton of satchels, opening them all up gets us up to item level 158. And actually, we're fully geared with at least the 171 item level blue drops from this. The only thing we're missing is trinkets, but those don't actually drop from the satchels. Maybe we can upgrade that during Brewfest, though. So, from here on out, we can try to minmax it by questing and going for the rare proced epic satchels to hopefully get a whole set of epic gear at item level 178, which could be worth it. For now, we'll take the upgrades and with the new set, revisit an old nemesis.

You already know, the Red Ridge mob of Null Faster. This mob is technically a Battle for Azeroth mob in Redidge, and with his scaled level, he killed us quite a few times over the months. But now I think it's time for our redemption. Oh yeah, the gear is looking pretty solid and whole feaster goes down. Not to mention, he does give us about 5,000 XP, which is maybe one of our better XP methods right now. paragraphs.text: Greetings, travelers, and welcome back to Goldbound. A challenge series in which we discover the map of Azeroth, exploring one zone at a time. Each new zone is only opened when we earn a "Wild " token in already opened zones, and then spin a random selection. In the last episode, we discovered the Hinterlands—a good area for archaeology, but for a stable gold farm, the hourly profit was surprisingly low. After some farming and checking the mail, we have less than 50,000 gold left, and another 200,000 need to be collected before we can open a new zone. So, travelers, welcome back to the Hinterlands, and let's see if this "dead zone" yields any profit today. By the way, as for why the Inner Lands are a " dead zone"—there are several reasons for that.

First, we have not found a stable source of gold here that would significantly change the situation. Additionally, there are several classic farming locations in the Hinterlands that were previously available and are now simply gone. We've already talked about the ghost mushrooms that have completely disappeared from this area, but that's not all. But more on that later. First, let 's head to Jintal'alor to the Troll Ruins, where, to be honest , there are several options for farming. Of course, the spider cave, where the ghost mushrooms used to be, is no longer there, but the spiders themselves remain inside —they can technically be farmed, but they don't respawn instantly, so we'll have to wait between clearing eight to twelve spiders. Aside from the slow clearing, there's really nothing valuable to farm from them, although they can technically drop regular green items or epic world drops.

But the trade goods— crispy spider legs (about 45 silver), large venom sacs (about one silver), small spider legs (13 silver), and thick web, which is the cheapest of the options (43 silver) —only bring in 63 gold per hour. Yes. And since we need another 200,000 gold per token, this would require 3,174 hours, or 132 days of continuous spider farming. So, spiders are not an option. Fortunately, Jintal'alor does n't have only them, because there is something else here - trolls. Namely, trolls, from which wildvine falls . According to Wowhead, the drop chance is very low, around 0.3%, which is of course rare, but historically groups that farm these mobs do a five-person hyperspawn farm of all the ruins, getting a bunch of kills per hour. We are, of course, testing on Goldie, so grouping for open world farming is not considered, but we can still test it. Even if I get one item for 300 kills, I can kill about 900 trolls per hour alone, and wild vine is very valuable, its price is 384 gold.

Not bad. According to Wowhead, most trolls drop it, but there's one type of troll that's a bit more interesting. So, when farming Wild Vine, we should focus on the skin-scrapers from the Vile Branch clan. These guys can drop a rare recipe and probably the best drop in the entire zone—a pattern for an iron breastplate with feathers. The recipe itself has an average price of around 40,000 gold, while a crafted breastplate, which requires the Leatherworking profession, goes for 5,000 gold. So I definitely want to farm at least two such drops. One to just sell the recipe, because 40,000 gold is about as much as we have right now , and the other to send to my crafter twin Golden Path, who happens to have a leather shop. So maybe it's not a dead zone after all? Well, don't rush, because there's a problem. During testing, although Wowhead says wild vine is in the drop tables, my data suggests otherwise. Thousands of trolls killed, but zero wild vines . Looking at the forums, I see that, as with the ghost mushroom, when the zone scaling in the Hinterlands changed, the level range went beyond the drop rate of Wild Vine, and with it, another option for farming gold in the Hinterlands disappeared. Not ideal.

So with that in mind, I'll call trolls neutral, but that's not all Jin'do the Curser has. In addition to the leatherworking recipe , there is also the second most valuable drop in the zone. It drops from a rare enemy at the top of the ruins, Mistress Enchantress. This rare enemy is the only one in the area with a specific item that, in my opinion, is worth ambushing. Other rare enemies are definitely worth killing for a cheap transmog, but this one drops Chan's Imperial Robe—a transmog item worth 20 to 40,000 gold. So, we currently have at least two notable drops in the area, and we definitely want to hunt this enemy down. And since it's really the only mob in this area worth hunting, we need something to do in the meantime, and luckily this week's sponsor, the Idle Obelisk Miner, is just the thing . If you're a fan of gold bound, gold farming, and slow but enjoyable progression, you should check this out. So, the whole point of this game is mining ore, making ingots from it , upgrading your stats, your crust so you can mine higher level ore to make even better ingots, and, well, you get the point, it's a lot like gold bound. There are also obelisks along the way that act as mini-bosses to check your stats, and there are also drones and bombs that speed up the collection.

So while we wait for rare mobs here, we can still farm ore. Oh yes. Aside from ore-based progression, this game has no advertising, either forced or optional, and is designed to be completely free with limited additional costs if the player so desires. So you can start playing without any ads or costs, and honestly, the game feels great progress and forward movement. I've been testing and playing it for a few weeks now , including on night flights, and I feel like I've barely scratched the surface. This is simply an extremely fun game for real " golden goblins", available on all platforms for any mobile device. So, if you want to try it out and support the channel at the same time , click the link in the description and download it today. That's all. After standing in AFK for a while, we finally got the tag and, in fact, the drop itself. A huge thank you to Idle Apocalypse Miner for sponsoring this video and, well, the chance at Imperial Robes. With a few notable items on the drop list, the area may not seem so bad. The problem is that even after receiving these items and knowing their value, we are unlikely to sell them quickly. And even if we sell, we still need some more gold for the token.

Of course, we will put the clothes up for sale in the hope of a quick deal , but we will need something more stable. Unfortunately, the time-forgotten farms of the Hinterlands don't end with wild vines or ghost mushrooms, not at all. Because the Skull Rock cave , where ghost mushrooms used to be , now has several other types of mobs roaming around. Jade slime and green slime. Historically, both of these mobs dropped Snail's Bag—a famous forgotten farm in the series. These are the same bags that dropped in the Swamp of Sorrow and the Swamps, but in the current version of the game, after reaching levels 30–50 , they stopped dropping due to the scaling of mobs and items. And, in fact, the Inner Lands are no different. So the Slug Bag, which is valuable because of the battle pet inside—the Abominable Slug—is also lost to this zone. No matter how many of these little slugs we destroy, we won't get this drop.

However, the news is not all bad, as the cave has decent ore deposits, so it's worth stopping by here from time to time during your herb gathering and mining routes to grab some ore. Honestly, I'm sure there are even more forgotten farms that I have n't even guessed about. Another type of farming that comes to mind is the old recurring quest in this zone, the Troll Necklace reward, which has also been removed, and as far as I know, the Zul'Farrak questline has also been removed from this zone . So, in the Hinterlands we only have a base for farming. As of now, we have a few local merchants, one of whom I still have in stock, two rare items, and, of course, double resource gathering, which is where it looks like we'll have to get the bulk of the gold. With that in mind, I continue my resource gathering rounds, and during them I check for rare enemies, as well as look for treasure chests in the area. The chests in this area can drop some pretty valuable blue items, and I want to collect as much loot here as possible.

As for herbs and ore, the income is usually less than 4000 gold per hour in pure form, so for now I'm just hoarding those supplies. I want to harvest as much as possible while I have these professions, and later in the week I will drop the harvesting professions and switch to production professions to hopefully increase our profits. Well, that was my plan for finishing this zone, but travelers , you saw the title of this video, and we have a lot to talk about, because right now, and a day or two after this video comes out, we're in the midst of BlizzCon season. And normally it wouldn't affect the Gold Bound challenge, but this time, oh, and how it does. Because look at this, the Winds of Mysterious Luck buff. This really changes everything.

Sure, gaining experience and reputation is nice, but what's really crazy for a challenge like Gold Bound is that every mob killed and quest completed, even in the Hinterlands and our open areas, has a chance to give us a mysterious satchel. Inside the satchel are all sorts of things, like experience potions tied to the account, but also equipment. This is not transmogrifiable equipment, it is completely character-bound and cannot be scattered, but a complete mystery set can be assembled. But the most important thing here is that this equipment adapts to the level at which you received the bag. So while we're running through these super low level zones at level 86 in level 30-70 gear from our zones, level 171-178 blue and epic items can drop from these bags . This is significantly better than any equipment we can currently obtain in our zones. So, theoretically, we can try to collect a full set of current equipment on Goldie while staying in our open areas. So let's start farming these bags.

There are several ways we can get them . First of all, there's a daily bonus where the first few mobs we kill simply give an epic satchel, and epic satchels always drop epic gear. Additionally, by killing mobs in the open world or dungeons after that first daily drop, we can randomly receive blue or epic satchels. Plus, completing quests can also yield suitcases. So let's check this out. Although it's worth noting while farming that this won't be an instant source of gold for Goldie. This is more of a preparation for future zones where mobs may be of a much higher level. We've already encountered strange scaling in the Uldaman : Tyr's Legacy dungeon, where mobs required a lot of hits to kill. And of course, the Redridge Devourer Spider, that is, the Redridge raid boss—if we collect the full set, we will definitely go for revenge. In a challenge like this, we usually just don't know what will happen with scaling.

It could change dramatically with the next addition and potential feature compression in the future. So while this limited- time event is going on, we really need to make the most of it. Having some experience in farming and testing these bags, in terms of their quantity per hour, there is a clear leader. I first tested this by simply killing trolls over and over again. And in an hour we only received two blue bags. Not very well. I even tried going through old dungeons like Uldaman for the high kill-per-hour rate to knock out more bags, but I didn't get any . The real king here is quests. Each quest completion gives one bag and about 2000 additional experience. Well, I say "every quest", but there are certain limitations . So, repetitive quests, daily tasks, or quests where you just go from point to point and don't complete any tasks, don't give bags, but regular zone quests do.

So let's focus and complete the rest of the quests in the Hinterlands for the bags. Okay, all the quests in the Hinterlands are complete and we have about 30 bags to open. Quests are definitely the best way. After collecting all the loot, we've filled quite a few gear slots, but we're still missing about four pieces of mysterious gear. Despite this, we raised our item level to 130 and more than doubled our health pool. Madness. Luckily, I still have some unfinished quests left in the Twilight Forest. We never finished these quests when we were in this area. So, by doing these old quests now, we get a bunch more bags, and after opening them, our item level increases to 158. What's more, we're fully equipped with at least a level 171 blue drop from this. The only thing we're missing is accessories, but they don't really fall out of the bags.

Maybe we can improve them during Hopfest. So from now on we can try to minimize by completing quests and hunting for rare epic bags to hopefully get a full set of level 178 epic gear, which might be worth it. For now, we'll accept these improvements and visit an old enemy with a new set. You already know, this is the mob in Redridge—Zul Firster. This mob is technically an enemy from Battle for Azeroth in Redridge, and due to its scalable level, it has killed us quite a few times in recent months. But now, I think, it's time for our payback.

Oh yes. The equipment looks pretty solid, and Firster falls. Not to mention that it gives us around 5000 experience, which is probably one of our best methods of gaining experience right now. We still have a few days to try to get epic upgrades, so hopefully they'll drop during our farm. But speaking of farming, we have a new update of raids that you need to complete. Since I'm still using double harvesting, I might skip some raids that require skinning, like Blackwing's Lair, this week . The first will be Onyxia's Lair, where there is a chance to get an Onyxia Dragon.

Ha. Yes, there is nothing here . But before we head to the Fiery Core, I can completely clear out the rare enemies in the Arat Highlands once more and try to get some of the Azerite set from BFA, maybe some mounts, and hopefully some pets to sell at auction. Okay, that's it. A Furry Crawler has fallen from Poisonous. If you lock him in a cage, it must cost several thousand gold. And the Fragment of Azzinoth, another battle favorite. We're pretty lucky with battle pets this time. Oh my god, another one, Angry Egg. So it's not a bad way to clear rare enemies in Arat. This is over, and it will be another two or three weeks before we can clear Arati again. As for the Seventh Legionnaire kit, we've also almost assembled a complete set. The only thing missing are the shoulder pads, so maybe next time we can complete it and get the full set.

This won't matter much until we get the Heart of Azeroth, which as far as I know requires unlocking Boralus and Battle for Azeroth, but it's good to have for the future. So, next we have none other than the Fiery Bore. Because we are still hunting the left side of Windseeker's Chain, and this is our 44th run. This week , however, I'll be doing a few regular mob cleanups to accumulate some more Black Iron Ore. We built up a huge stockpile of this a few months ago and reworked it all into black iron items. And several of these items have actually managed to sell in recent weeks. So soon we'll have to create a bunch of these things on our viola again. So let's get some black iron for this. But, of course, the main thing we're here for is Baron Haddon and his left shackle. Is this the same week?

Well, no. But hey, at least we have this Black Iron Ore to smelt. And while we're at it , we might as well finish setting up the Fiery Cores in the Depths of Black Mountain. This way we can just jump into the teleportation window in the Fiery Core, instead of having to talk to the NPC every time . Once all the Dark Iron ore is smelted, we can set it aside and turn in the customization quest, which actually raises us to level 87 and gives us another bag. So, let 's open it. Oh, oh. Do you see that? It seems like the level of items in the bags actually scales based on your level at the time you get the bag. And since we've hit level 87, the blue items are now nine levels higher and even better than our old level 86 epic stuff, which unfortunately means that almost all of our epic set is now outdated and needs to be replaced.

But in reality, if we continue to gain experience in this way during the event, it will happen again at levels 88 and 89 . So, travelers, I think I know what we should do. We need to quickly level Goldie up to level 89 before the event ends and get a full set of epic gear of the highest possible level. We have until the 23rd, so I think it's technically possible. But with that in mind, we can't use bags for leveling up because we have a limited number of unfinished tasks in unlocked areas. Since recurring quests like daily quests don't give bags, I really want to save the zone quests for level 89 to have the best chance of getting a full set of gear. Because, as it turns out, if you get to level 90, equipment will no longer drop from your bags . So, 89 is the peak. Ultimately, I think we are left with three options for leveling up. We still gain experience from gathering resources, ore, and herbs, which is how we've leveled up so far, and it's been incredibly slow. Since a level requires 550,000 experience and each node gives 124 units, that's about 45 hours of continuous resource gathering per level.

Not very fast. Then there is the Null Feaster, a rare spider. We can definitely kill him repeatedly now, and each kill gives us a full 5,000–6,000 experience. As testing has shown , it appears with a reliable 6- minute respawn timer. So, with proper efficiency, that's 60,000 experience per hour, about 10 hours per level. Not bad, but, travelers, I think we can do better. An area of ​​the game that we haven't fully explored yet on Goldi: pet battles. So we're back at Donna Antia's, the crazy cat lady here in Alvin, this time to stock up on troops. We also received a few new pets from Maroti today, which may end up in our battle inventory rather than the auction. So, the idea is this. I have a hunch that pet battles will bring the most experience per hour for Goldie, and if we also level up some of them from level 1 to 25, this will significantly affect their price at the auction. In many cases, a level 25 battle pet sells either for more or much faster than a level 1 pet. We're currently limited in locations, and there are other ways to level up pets much faster that we don't have access to, so our open world battles may be a little inefficient, but some level 25 pets cost a few thousand gold more than the first.

So if we can level Goldie up a bit to level 89 and earn some gold at the same time, I think it's a pretty good deal. Defeating any battle pet in the open world gives Goldie experience, although at low levels from 1 to 3 it is not that much. Therefore, I will have to level up my team of battle pets to around level 17 to be able to fight in our zone with the highest level pets—the Scorched Lands. I think that's where we'll really get the most experience per hour in the open world. Additionally, we have combat pet trainers in each zone. Since we've already progressed quite far through the Eastern Kingdoms, we have several areas with trainers offering daily challenges. These trainers are now adjusting to the highest level of your combat pets. So if I have a team of three trainees of the same level, we will fight against a trainer at the same level. That's why we need to maintain approximately the same level of our team during leveling.

During the passage, each trainer will give us experience for victory, as well as about 15,000 experience for the daily task, which also scales with the buff from the mysterious prophet. So rest assured, in the next few days we will be hosting a world tour of combat pet trainers. I'll try to put together a good team and see how it goes. Okay, that definitely works. A few hours have passed and we are already at level 88. In addition, the next day has arrived, so all the trainers' daily tasks have been updated. With a little experience, my current battle strategy is to use Fozeling, the pet we got from Fozvar in Arat Highlands this week. He simply has a powerful starting combination between defense and Earthquake, which hits all enemy pets, even those in the rear. So, starting with Fosling, we deal significant damage to their entire team. Then we can change the pets to spares and finish them off with the rest of the team. But for now, these are all combat pet trainers, and we are already confidently walking towards level 88. Although, looking at our pet journal, I think they're ready to head out to the farms in the Scorched Earth. This is our current zone with the highest level of battles, so the best experience should be here. Oh, yes. Each battle win here gives us about 6–8k experience, and since we can fight one battle in 1–3 minutes, if I focus for a few hours, we should reach level 89 and be able to go get the rest of the gear. And here it is . A few hours of pet battles are behind us, and although our pets haven't quite reached level 25, we've taken 89th. And, you know, that's enough for me right now. I can always level up these pets later by completing daily quests, but right now I want to maximize wins and mystery bags at level 89, because once we hit 90, the gear will stop dropping.

So, we went to complete the quests. Since I haven't really progressed through the storylines in some of these zones, the Scorched Lands and Swamp of Sorrows are the closest to visit, so let's tackle those. OK. Well, it didn't take long to complete a bunch of quests and fill an entire deep-sea bag with backpacks, and even more. So let's start opening the bags. Current item level is 161, and we have 202,000 health. Let's open them and see how much it will improve our equipment. Starting with the blue ones, those at level 89 actually scale up to level 198 . This is much better than our old epics, so I think grinding to level 89 is worth it. One of the epics is actually item level 205. I didn't think we'd have such a high item level in Golden Bonds a few more additions, but after equipping we were actually lucky enough to collect a full set of blue gear, as well as a few epic items, which brought our total item level to 179 and health to 264k . So I think we are relatively prepared for the future. I'll definitely try to replace as many of these blue items with epic ones over the next few days, but right now our weakest points are accessories. Although we may be able to improve them faster than expected. But we've been distracted by side quests for long enough, leveling up and getting gear, so let's take this new gear, which is probably the best for us, and head back to the Hinterlands, because gold won't farm itself. By the way, there's one thing I want to check out on the farm in this area, especially since the Winter Veil Festival is coming up pretty soon.

Owls, which are literally everywhere in this area, look like munchkins. There are two types of them: wild and ferocious, but for us they are the same, because we are only interested in one thing - again, small eggs. Now, the spawn area of ​​these creatures is so large that we don't have to worry about respawn speed or routes, and we can use acceleration and grappling hooks to move well and get a good number of kills per hour. In fact, these guys cover almost the entire map, which is both good and bad. This is good for farming, but means there aren't many different mobs here, other than them, trolls, some slugs, and maybe turtles on the coast. So we definitely want to test them while we're here, because after all, there's nothing much else to farm in this zone .

Regarding the metrics, I thought it would farm less than 1000 gold per hour, but I'm honestly pleasantly surprised. We are getting about 350 small eggs per hour, which is significantly better than our initial farm in Reddridge, but not as good as Westfall or Loch Modan. At current market prices, that's about 2,450 gold per hour from eggs alone. And who knows, egg prices might jump a bit in the future. During the last Winter Veil, they rose to 100 gold for a while, stabilized around 15 gold during the event, but dropped to eight pretty quickly. Aside from the small eggs here, we really only get gray hollow wing bones and the occasional green transmogrification item. But, hey, not a bad farm for this zone.

At least the small eggs still drop here, unlike many other items in this area. But having said all that, travelers, it's time to check your email. As you already know, WoW has had some big announcements lately, and they've, well , raised the price of our token from around 250,000 gold to almost 300k at the moment. So let's hope that mailboxes will be emptied quite significantly. There are lots of different kinds of goods to trade, mostly from the zone, but also from the New Moon Fair that was held this week. So, let's get all this out of the mail. So, on trade goods alone, we have almost 72,000 gold. If some large leftover transmogrification items sell, we could stock up for a new zone.

Looking at the first character for transmogrification, it doesn't seem like anything special sold. In fact, the last few weeks have been quite challenging for transmogrification. Let's quickly take all this away. And that's over 30,000 gold on transmogrification, which, overall, isn't bad at all. How about a character in the Hinterlands? Silence. Well, after sending all of this to Goldie, we have 107,000 gold, which is something. But with a token price of almost 300k, we'll have to act more decisively if we ever want to get a new zone. For now, go with honor, my friend.
I know.
